name: Mary Peltola
subject: We will keep fighting until every ballot is counted
body:
| | | | I wanted you to get this update from me: **Ballots are still being counted, and right now, it’s still too close to call.** We are going to do everything we can to make sure every single vote is counted in this race. But I’ll be honest: That is going to take time – and plenty of resources that we don’t currently have. As we fight to make sure every ballot is counted, we’re going to remain the top target of the DC establishment. We put everything we had into winning this race, so I’m counting on your help to fight back against their attacks. It looks like we’re in this for the long haul, so I need your help to sustain our fight until every vote is counted. From the very beginning, this campaign has been powered by grassroots donations from people like you. I’m proud of that fact, but it means it’s going to take lots of us to stand up to their pressure in the coming days. That’s why I have to ask: [**If you can afford it today, please pitch in anything you can to my and Tobias Read'****s campaign at this critical moment. But your answer matters to me.
Because while the pundits and political insiders spend the next few months debating what Democrats _should do_ , **I'd rather hear from the people we're actually supposed to be working for.**
And I want you to know something else.
**I'm heading into this new Congress with my sleeves rolled up, my priorities straight, and every intention of making the most of this opportunity.**
There are going to be big fights ahead. There will be tough conversations, long days, and probably quite a few mornings where the trees back home in Vermont are going to hear ALL about the things I can't believe I have to explain to grown adults in Congress.
But there's also an incredible opportunity to make real progress for the people who have been waiting far too long for someone to put their needs first.
**And I intend to make every single day count.**
So tell me what's on your mind. I’m all ears.
With love and determination,

On April 18, 1945, I walked up to my squadron commander and said, "This is my 75th mission. Don't you think it's time to quit?"He said, "Yeah. This is going to be your last mission."He was right. _Just not the way either of us meant._ My name is Wally King. I just turned 103. During World War II, I flew P-47 Thunderbolts over France and Germany with the 513th Fighter Squadron.

I grew up in rural Ohio. I went to all 12 grades in the same school building, and my graduating class had 32 students. All 16 of the boys served in the war.I'd wanted to fly since I was a kid building model airplanes. The P-47 was a tough, honest airplane. It could take a beating and bring you home.The mission I remember most came just before Christmas 1944, during the Battle of the Bulge.Our job was to knock out the German guns around Bastogne before the supply planes came in. Everything was buried in snow.When the parachutes dropped, men who had been dug in under all that white came up out of the ground and started dragging those supplies into town.**Patriot, I'll never forget that sight.** _Then came April 18._ On the way home, my wingman spotted a gun on a railroad car, and we went down for a look. Flak hit my engine. Fire came over the windshield.I bailed out over German territory with civilians shooting at me on the way down.Patriot, I was beaten, burned and terrified. I'd never given God much thought before that day, but right then, a peace came over me like nothing I'd ever felt. It stayed with me the whole two weeks I was a prisoner.**And it was a German doctor who got me home.** He was caring for badly wounded Americans in a house near the Russian front. When the war was all but over, he rode with us in two ambulances to the American lines, driving after midnight with no lights.I've often wondered how many of those boys would have lived without him.

For years now, I've talked to students about the war.**What troubles me, Patriot, is how little young Americans know about World War II.** When students ask me for advice, I tell them: _put down your cell phones and love one another._ But I can't get to every classroom, Patriot.**That's why I'm writing to you on behalf of the American Veterans Center. They make sure the next generation hears the truth from the people who lived it.** AVC is a nonprofit educational organization dedicated to preserving and promoting the legacy of America's veterans and active-duty service members, from World War II through today. Its work includes:
---
* **The National Memorial Day Parade** in Washington, D.C., the nation's largest Memorial Day event
* **The Annual Veterans Conference** every Veterans Day weekend, where veterans of every generation share their stories with hundreds of cadets and midshipmen
* **AMERICAN VALOR: A Salute to Our Heroes,** a two-time Emmy-winning special broadcast nationwide
* **Oral histories and documentaries** that record veterans' stories in their own words, so they're never lost

---

clean_body: My commander was right. Just not the way either of us meant. | | | | Patriot, On April 18, 1945, I walked up to my squadron commander and said, "This is my 75th mission. Don't you think it's time to quit?"He said, "Yeah. This is going to be your last mission."He was right. Just not the way either of us meant. My name is Wally King. I just turned 103. During World War II, I flew P-47 Thunderbolts over France and Germany with the 513th Fighter Squadron. I grew up in rural Ohio. I went to all 12 grades in the same school building, and my graduating class had 32 students. All 16 of the boys served in the war.I'd wanted to fly since I was a kid building model airplanes. The P-47 was a tough, honest airplane. It could take a beating and bring you home.The mission I remember most came just before Christmas 1944, during the Battle of the Bulge.Our job was to knock out the German guns around Bastogne before the supply planes came in. Everything was buried in snow.When the parachutes dropped, men who had been dug in under all that white came up out of the ground and started dragging those supplies into town.Patriot, I'll never forget that sight. Then came April 18. On the way home, my wingman spotted a gun on a railroad car, and we went down for a look. Flak hit my engine. Fire came over the windshield.I bailed out over German territory with civilians shooting at me on the way down.Patriot, I was beaten, burned and terrified. I'd never given God much thought before that day, but right then, a peace came over me like nothing I'd ever felt. It stayed with me the whole two weeks I was a prisoner.And it was a German doctor who got me home. He was caring for badly wounded Americans in a house near the Russian front. When the war was all but over, he rode with us in two ambulances to the American lines, driving after midnight with no lights.I've often wondered how many of those boys would have lived without him. Above: I met with the boys of the 117 th Air Refueling Wing of the Alabama National Guard before flying to Normandy, France in June 2025 for the 81 st anniversary of D-Day. For years now, I've talked to students about the war.What troubles me, Patriot, is how little young Americans know about World War II. When students ask me for advice, I tell them: put down your cell phones and love one another. But I can't get to every classroom, Patriot.That's why I'm writing to you on behalf of the American Veterans Center. They make sure the next generation hears the truth from the people who lived it. AVC is a nonprofit educational organization dedicated to preserving and promoting the legacy of America's veterans and active-duty service members, from World War II through today. Its work includes: The National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C., the nation's largest Memorial Day event The Annual Veterans Conference every Veterans Day weekend, where veterans of every generation share their stories with hundreds of cadets and midshipmen AMERICAN VALOR: A Salute to Our Heroes, a two-time Emmy-winning special broadcast nationwide Oral histories and documentaries that record veterans' stories in their own words, so they're never lost AVC is funded entirely by people like you, and every gift is tax-deductible. Thank you for listening to an old pilot - and for taking the time to consider supporting the American Veterans Center. I hope you'll join them on this mission to honor our veterans by preserving and promoting their legacies of service and sacrifice. Wally King First Lieutenant, U.S. Army Air Forces 513th Fighter Squadron, 406th Fighter Group, Ninth Air ForceOn behalf of American Veterans Center, P.S. Patriot, my commander promised me one last mission back in 1945. At 103, I've found another one: making sure young Americans know the truth about war and the brave veterans who fought to keep America free throughout history. | | | The mission of the American Veterans Center and the World War II Veterans Committee is to preserve and promote the legacy and experiences of America's veterans and active duty service personnel from World War II through today. ---|---|---
A Palm Beach Sheriff's Office deputy attempts to remove Nihaya Atchanah during the public comments portion during a Palm Beach County Board of County Commissioners meeting in downtown West Palm Beach, Fla., on October 6, 2026. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect.
Palm Beach County, Florida, the world's largest government investor in Israeli government bonds, held nearly a quarter of its investment portfolio in Israeli bonds before $67.5 million of the securities matured on November 1, far exceeding its own investment limits. The county did not reinvest the proceeds because its existing holdings were already above the permitted ceiling, according to its interim comptroller. The repayment reduced the county's exposure but left 22.5% of its portfolio invested in Israeli government debt, still above the allowed investment cap of 15%.
The investments had prompted months of protests by residents, who have also faced arrests and removal from public meetings while attempting to challenge the county's financial support for Israel.
At a September 15 budget hearing, Palestinian American legal scholar and human rights attorney Noura Erakat was [arrested and charged](https://substack.com/redirect/8c0f8e11-5a4e-4fa9-8c4a-259ec219d67a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with misdemeanor trespassing after refusing orders to leave the chamber. Sheriff's deputies also removed other attendees who had sought to speak against the investments. County officials had limited public comment to one minute per speaker and ruled discussion of Israel bonds outside the scope of the budget hearing. Erakat and civil rights organizations condemned the arrest as an infringement on free speech, while county officials maintained that investment policy was not on the hearing's agenda.
Lydia Ghuman, executive director of the Internationalist Law Center, accused county officials of using vague public-comment rules to suppress opposition to the investments. The rules allow officials to curtail comments for conduct deemed "disruptive" or that "obstructs the meeting progress," language that officials use to target criticism of Israel bonds, Ghuman said. "They now use this as grounds to ensure you can be taken away by the sheriff and the microphone silenced," she told Drop Site.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/671d86e4-af22-4d43-8cad-6e261b5fdd8e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Former Palm Beach County Clerk Michael Caruso announces another round of Israel bond investments, pushing the total to $1 billion or 17% of the county total investment portfolio, on January 7, 2026. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect.
Interim Clerk and Comptroller Shannon Ramsey-Chessman, who assumed the position after the former County Clerk Michael Caruso was suspended following his August [arrest](https://substack.com/redirect/a9c512ee-926e-4259-8925-760a924c249f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on child sexual abuse charges, confirmed in a statement to Drop Site News that Israeli government bonds represented 24.2% of the county's investment portfolio immediately before November 1, falling to 22.5% after the $67.5 million maturity. Caruso has pleaded not guilty to the child sex abuse charges.
"Because we will continue to be at the policy's maximum allowable investment percentage after the maturity of $67.5 million in bonds on November 1, we are not permitted to reinvest at this time," Ramsey-Chessman told Drop Site in an earlier statement. "However, we will review reinvesting once we may do so within the compliance cap."
The last development in the Palm Beach divestment fight comes amid a growing national campaign to withdraw public money from investments connected to Israel. In Providence, Rhode Island, more than 76% of voters on November 3 [approved](https://substack.com/redirect/91ce15c8-e16d-438f-855a-89eddb10cc41?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a ballot measure requiring the city "to divest from countries and companies profiting from genocide, apartheid, ethnic cleansing, and prolonged military occupation." Organizers describe it as the first binding municipal divestment law approved directly by voters.
In Massachusetts, Cambridge's city council [voted](https://substack.com/redirect/864712af-b580-4585-8dcd-afe1e9fdea0e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on October 28 to divest $24 million in municipal funds from companies associated with apartheid and genocide, while Easthampton's council unanimously adopted a divestment resolution on October 22. Somerville is scheduled to consider a binding boycott and divestment ordinance on November 12, following voter approval of a divestment ballot question last year.
More than 30 U.S. cities, counties, and states have taken divestment measures over the past three years, according to the Internationalist Law Center.
"These divestment wins across the country signal that Israel bonds, and genocide, are in fact poor investments that harm taxpayers," said Ghuman.
The county's holdings, which reached approximately $1 billion in January, fell to roughly $932.5 million following the repayment, assuming no other changes in principal. But the new figures raise questions about how Palm Beach County came to hold such a large concentration of public funds in Israeli government debt, even as officials repeatedly sought to increase the limits governing those investments.
Ramsey-Chessman defended the county's investment practices, saying the clerk's office had always evaluated investments according to three factors: safety, liquidity, and rate of return.
"Our previous investments in Israel Bonds were focused on the significant investment income for county taxpayers, at a time when other investment opportunities were not performing at the same level," she said.
The county's repeated efforts to increase the investment ceiling have also raised questions about whether the investments were motivated solely by financial considerations.
The investments expanded under former Clerk and Comptroller Joseph Abruzzo, who publicly described them as reflecting the county's commitment to Israel.
Ramsey-Chessman attributed the unusually high percentage of Israel bonds in the portfolio to changes in the county's investment policy and seasonal fluctuations in the amount of money available for investment.
"Keep in mind that when we made our last purchase in March, the allowable cap was 18%, and we invested up to that cap," Ramsey-Chessman said.
The county receives most of its property tax revenue in late November and December, she explained, leaving its investment portfolio at its lowest point of the year before those payments arrive. As the overall portfolio shrinks, Israel bonds account for a larger percentage of its value, even without additional purchases, according to the interim comptroller.
## "Not Really Good Practice"
Tom Sgouros, a municipal finance expert, said seasonal fluctuations in tax revenues are predictable, but the larger concern is the county's concentration of investments in a single issuer. "It's not really good practice to hold a quarter of your investment portfolio in one investment, period," he told Drop Site News. "Diversification does not mean buying different bond issues from the same issuer."
The county's investment policy measures the allowable percentage of Israel bonds at the time of purchase. That means a subsequent increase in their share of the portfolio does not necessarily constitute a violation of the purchase restriction. Nevertheless, the figures show that nearly a quarter of the county's investment portfolio was concentrated in Israeli government debt before the November repayment, a level substantially above the current ceiling intended to limit such exposure.
An [investigation](https://substack.com/redirect/a058f50d-34ee-4ad6-8517-c9e1dbbd7f7b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by Colby Donovan published last month revealed that Palm Beach County exceeded its own investment limits when purchasing Israel bonds on three occasions since January 2024. On January 6, 2026, the county purchased $350.5 million in Israeli government bonds, bringing its holdings to $1 billion, or 20.04% of its investment portfolio, despite an 18% cap. The investigation, based on county trade records and custodian reports, found that the county exceeded its allowable allocation by approximately $101.7 million. It also found that the county's automated compliance checks did not monitor Israel bonds as a percentage of the overall portfolio.
In October 2025, the county commission approved a temporary increase in the allowable Israel bonds allocation from 15% to 18%, permitting further purchases before the limit was scheduled to revert to 15%. In February, the county's Investment Policy Committee considered making the higher ceiling permanent. That proposal failed in a 3-3 vote, although the committee approved a temporary extension of the 18% limit through March 2.
Last month, Palm Beach residents and organizers said they had persuaded two members of the county's Investment Policy Committee to [vote against](https://substack.com/redirect/2af0fbdd-590a-4fb0-9c23-bcd9b8e64c9a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a proposal to increase the allotment to 20%. Campaign organizers met with Ramsey-Chessman and her staff on October 15 to present their objections to the investments.
But the November non-reinvestment was not a discretionary divestment decision. Ramsey-Chessman said the existing investment cap prohibited the clerk's office from purchasing additional Israel bonds, regardless of the campaign's demands. The October 15 committee vote had [preserved](https://substack.com/redirect/b409f977-83b8-4d6b-a50c-6fa71f260dad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that restriction by rejecting a proposal to raise the cap from 15% to 20%.
The county is scheduled to receive repayments on four additional occasions: January 2027, February 2027, March 2027, and August 2028. If those payments are also allowed to mature without reinvestment, the county could eventually eliminate its entire portfolio.
The November repayment came just two days before voters[ elected](https://substack.com/redirect/dd5a6295-6a17-4c07-bd15-1d1d864bada7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Democrat Yvette Drucker, a former Boca Raton deputy mayor, as the county's new clerk and comptroller. Drucker defeated Michael Caruso, the suspended incumbent.
Drucker, who was scheduled to take office November 10,[ campaigned](https://substack.com/redirect/23151e58-5321-471c-80b6-d29a18f8ad70?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on maintaining the county's investments in Israel bonds, but has also said she would evaluate investments based on financial considerations rather than political or ideological tests. She will oversee future investment decisions involving the county's remaining holdings.
Palm Beach residents, including Palestinian Americans whose family members were killed or displaced in Gaza, challenged the county's investments in Israel bonds, arguing in a lawsuit that local public money should not finance the Israeli government and that officials were making investment decisions for political rather than financial reasons.
The residents' legal challenge was dismissed in July, when Palm Beach County Circuit Judge Glenn Kelley ruled that the plaintiffs had not established sufficient grounds to bring a taxpayer lawsuit. Their attorneys [appealed](https://substack.com/redirect/64bc8d67-82ec-4219-ae23-2b17e989b1ae?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in late August.
"Our tax dollars are supposed to be used for the benefit of our own community, and I believe that the Comptroller did not have our community's best interest in mind when he made these investments," one of the plaintiffs, identified in court documents as Jane Doe, said in a sworn declaration.

If you value this work, | | ---|---|--- A Palm Beach Sheriff's Office deputy attempts to remove Nihaya Atchanah during the public comments portion during a Palm Beach County Board of County Commissioners meeting in downtown West Palm Beach, Fla., on October 6, 2026. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect. Palm Beach County, Florida, the world's largest government investor in Israeli government bonds, held nearly a quarter of its investment portfolio in Israeli bonds before $67.5 million of the securities matured on November 1, far exceeding its own investment limits. The county did not reinvest the proceeds because its existing holdings were already above the permitted ceiling, according to its interim comptroller. The repayment reduced the county's exposure but left 22.5% of its portfolio invested in Israeli government debt, still above the allowed investment cap of 15%. The investments had prompted months of protests by residents, who have also faced arrests and removal from public meetings while attempting to challenge the county's financial support for Israel. At a September 15 budget hearing, Palestinian American legal scholar and human rights attorney Noura Erakat was with misdemeanor trespassing after refusing orders to leave the chamber. Sheriff's deputies also removed other attendees who had sought to speak against the investments. County officials had limited public comment to one minute per speaker and ruled discussion of Israel bonds outside the scope of the budget hearing. Erakat and civil rights organizations condemned the arrest as an infringement on free speech, while county officials maintained that investment policy was not on the hearing's agenda. Lydia Ghuman, executive director of the Internationalist Law Center, accused county officials of using vague public-comment rules to suppress opposition to the investments. The rules allow officials to curtail comments for conduct deemed "disruptive" or that "obstructs the meeting progress," language that officials use to target criticism of Israel bonds, Ghuman said. "They now use this as grounds to ensure you can be taken away by the sheriff and the microphone silenced," she told Drop Site. | | ---|---|--- Former Palm Beach County Clerk Michael Caruso announces another round of Israel bond investments, pushing the total to $1 billion or 17% of the county total investment portfolio, on January 7, 2026. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect. Interim Clerk and Comptroller Shannon Ramsey-Chessman, who assumed the position after the former County Clerk Michael Caruso was suspended following his August on child sexual abuse charges, confirmed in a statement to Drop Site News that Israeli government bonds represented 24.2% of the county's investment portfolio immediately before November 1, falling to 22.5% after the $67.5 million maturity. Caruso has pleaded not guilty to the child sex abuse charges. "Because we will continue to be at the policy's maximum allowable investment percentage after the maturity of $67.5 million in bonds on November 1, we are not permitted to reinvest at this time," Ramsey-Chessman told Drop Site in an earlier statement. "However, we will review reinvesting once we may do so within the compliance cap." The last development in the Palm Beach divestment fight comes amid a growing national campaign to withdraw public money from investments connected to Israel. In Providence, Rhode Island, more than 76% of voters on November 3 a ballot measure requiring the city "to divest from countries and companies profiting from genocide, apartheid, ethnic cleansing, and prolonged military occupation." Organizers describe it as the first binding municipal divestment law approved directly by voters. In Massachusetts, Cambridge's city council on October 28 to divest $24 million in municipal funds from companies associated with apartheid and genocide, while Easthampton's council unanimously adopted a divestment resolution on October 22. Somerville is scheduled to consider a binding boycott and divestment ordinance on November 12, following voter approval of a divestment ballot question last year. More than 30 U.S. cities, counties, and states have taken divestment measures over the past three years, according to the Internationalist Law Center. "These divestment wins across the country signal that Israel bonds, and genocide, are in fact poor investments that harm taxpayers," said Ghuman. The county's holdings, which reached approximately $1 billion in January, fell to roughly $932.5 million following the repayment, assuming no other changes in principal. But the new figures raise questions about how Palm Beach County came to hold such a large concentration of public funds in Israeli government debt, even as officials repeatedly sought to increase the limits governing those investments. Ramsey-Chessman defended the county's investment practices, saying the clerk's office had always evaluated investments according to three factors: safety, liquidity, and rate of return. "Our previous investments in Israel Bonds were focused on the significant investment income for county taxpayers, at a time when other investment opportunities were not performing at the same level," she said. The county's repeated efforts to increase the investment ceiling have also raised questions about whether the investments were motivated solely by financial considerations. The investments expanded under former Clerk and Comptroller Joseph Abruzzo, who publicly described them as reflecting the county's commitment to Israel. Ramsey-Chessman attributed the unusually high percentage of Israel bonds in the portfolio to changes in the county's investment policy and seasonal fluctuations in the amount of money available for investment. "Keep in mind that when we made our last purchase in March, the allowable cap was 18%, and we invested up to that cap," Ramsey-Chessman said. The county receives most of its property tax revenue in late November and December, she explained, leaving its investment portfolio at its lowest point of the year before those payments arrive. As the overall portfolio shrinks, Israel bonds account for a larger percentage of its value, even without additional purchases, according to the interim comptroller. "Not Really Good Practice" Tom Sgouros, a municipal finance expert, said seasonal fluctuations in tax revenues are predictable, but the larger concern is the county's concentration of investments in a single issuer. "It's not really good practice to hold a quarter of your investment portfolio in one investment, period," he told Drop Site News. "Diversification does not mean buying different bond issues from the same issuer." The county's investment policy measures the allowable percentage of Israel bonds at the time of purchase. That means a subsequent increase in their share of the portfolio does not necessarily constitute a violation of the purchase restriction. Nevertheless, the figures show that nearly a quarter of the county's investment portfolio was concentrated in Israeli government debt before the November repayment, a level substantially above the current ceiling intended to limit such exposure. An by Colby Donovan published last month revealed that Palm Beach County exceeded its own investment limits when purchasing Israel bonds on three occasions since January 2024. On January 6, 2026, the county purchased $350.5 million in Israeli government bonds, bringing its holdings to $1 billion, or 20.04% of its investment portfolio, despite an 18% cap. The investigation, based on county trade records and custodian reports, found that the county exceeded its allowable allocation by approximately $101.7 million. It also found that the county's automated compliance checks did not monitor Israel bonds as a percentage of the overall portfolio. In October 2025, the county commission approved a temporary increase in the allowable Israel bonds allocation from 15% to 18%, permitting further purchases before the limit was scheduled to revert to 15%. In February, the county's Investment Policy Committee considered making the higher ceiling permanent. That proposal failed in a 3-3 vote, although the committee approved a temporary extension of the 18% limit through March 2. Last month, Palm Beach residents and organizers said they had persuaded two members of the county's Investment Policy Committee to a proposal to increase the allotment to 20%. Campaign organizers met with Ramsey-Chessman and her staff on October 15 to present their objections to the investments. But the November non-reinvestment was not a discretionary divestment decision. Ramsey-Chessman said the existing investment cap prohibited the clerk's office from purchasing additional Israel bonds, regardless of the campaign's demands. The October 15 committee vote had that restriction by rejecting a proposal to raise the cap from 15% to 20%. The county is scheduled to receive repayments on four additional occasions: January 2027, February 2027, March 2027, and August 2028. If those payments are also allowed to mature without reinvestment, the county could eventually eliminate its entire portfolio. The November repayment came just two days before voters Democrat Yvette Drucker, a former Boca Raton deputy mayor, as the county's new clerk and comptroller. Drucker defeated Michael Caruso, the suspended incumbent. Drucker, who was scheduled to take office November 10, on maintaining the county's investments in Israel bonds, but has also said she would evaluate investments based on financial considerations rather than political or ideological tests. She will oversee future investment decisions involving the county's remaining holdings. Palm Beach residents, including Palestinian Americans whose family members were killed or displaced in Gaza, challenged the county's investments in Israel bonds, arguing in a lawsuit that local public money should not finance the Israeli government and that officials were making investment decisions for political rather than financial reasons. The residents' legal challenge was dismissed in July, when Palm Beach County Circuit Judge Glenn Kelley ruled that the plaintiffs had not established sufficient grounds to bring a taxpayer lawsuit. O'Keefe Defense Fund - Legal Update

Patriot,

I've been deposed more times than I can count.

I've sat across the table from attorneys whose entire assignment was to intimidate me, confuse me, and convince me to quit. So when I say I understand how this game operates, I mean it.

Back in 2020, one of those depositions was captured on video. I recently released part of that footage, and I want you to understand what happened.

I told the lawyers exactly what I thought: “You brought me here against my will. You're the one suing us. You're the ones admitting that you're using this as a device to stop us.”

Then I made a promise: “So help me God, I will not stop fighting.”

And the lawyer's response?
“Well, we think you're a national disgrace, Mr. O'Keefe.”

Let that sink in. That is the attitude of the attorneys on the other side of the table.

body:
Tomorrow, we take off. Here’s how to make sure The Georgia Flyover lands in your inbox.

| | |
---
You're officially part of _The Georgia Flyover_ Crew. Welcome aboard! ✈️ We're glad you're here. Starting tomorrow, you can expect _The Georgia Flyover_ in your inbox each morning--a quick, engaging rundown of the Georgia stories worth knowing, along with the biggest national headlines impacting the Peach State. It's designed to give you the important stuff without taking up your whole morning. And yes, **it 's free.** Want to see what you signed up for? [You can read our latest Georgia edition here.](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJxsz7FuwyAQgOGngS3WHWDAA0MXb-na0aJwxki4jvA1Vd--ambvvz7p_7gv91hb_SrvcafAZV2-T-qLAmVviDfUMgcNmdB4SQHdZMbRaUC5BZqIVm1WMphGlz6jVdbSlEyCnIFQ1vDPIKIGDx794EeL3oB20dkIZIUBypWPPvBGhY5ealzb7_GkPqRjly1szI9T6DehZqHmy0qouUWmk4WaZQ_58VNbq6d1wkDZY20vii_fnkH9BQAA__8rE0-n) Before we send you on your way, we have one small favor to ask.
### Help us make sure _The Georgia Flyover_ actually lands in your inbox
Email providers sometimes have a mind of their own, especially when you've just subscribed to something new. Taking a minute to tell your inbox you _want_ to hear from us can help make sure tomorrow's _Georgia Flyover_ doesn't get lost along the way. **The easiest thing you can do?** Hit reply to this email and let us know you got it. Even a quick "Got it!" will do. Then, depending on which email service you use, here's one more step you can take: **Gmail**
* **On your phone:** Tap the three dots (...) in the top-right corner, choose "Move to," then select "Primary." If you don't see Primary as an option, you're already set.
* **On desktop:** Go back to your inbox and drag this email into the "Primary" tab.

**Apple Mail**
* Tap our email address at the top of this email (next to "From:" on mobile), then select "Add to VIP."

**AOL Mail**
* Select "Contacts," then "New Contact." Add [news@editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com](mailto:news@editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com) and save it as a contact.

**Outlook**
* Hover over our email address at the top of this email, click the three dots, choose "Add to Outlook Contacts," then click "Save" or "Create."

**Use something else?** [You can find instructions for your email provider here.](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJxsz79ugzAQgPGnsbegO_9n8NCFLV07Ihcf5iQTIuMk6ttX7Zz900_6vq7zNXHlW_lMO8Ve1vlxUpsVKHdBvKCWOWrIhCZIiuhHY63XgHKLq1k06TEY42iEMX8vdoXsIYG1eUEtOf4xiKghQMAwBOswGNA-eZeAnDBAmfvRhr5RoaMVTmv9OZ7UhuXYZY1b7_dT6A-hJqGmt5VQ02vjTpXPzrdyKQ_OJNQkW8z3F9fKp_PCQNkT13-2v_18RvUbAAD__6pmU68) And that's it. You're ready for takeoff. One last thing: **we really do want to hear from you.** If you have feedback, a Georgia story you think we should cover, or just want to tell us what you think of _The Georgia Flyover_ , email our Editor anytime at [editor@thegeorgiaflyover.com.com](mailto:editor@jointheflyover.com?subject=Feedback%20for%20The%20Georgia%20Flyover). Thanks for joining us. We'll see you in your inbox!

| Law Enforcement Legal Defense Fund I'm a wife and a mother, not an activist. But today I'm asking for your help because the man I love is facing the fight of his life. | | | |
---
| | | Dear Fellow Patriot, I never imagined I would be writing a letter like this. I'm a wife and a mother, not an activist. But today I'm asking for your help because the man I love is facing the fight of his life. My husband, Officer Brad Lunsford, will soon be back in court defending himself against charges that never should have been brought in the first place. And the legal bills continue to pile up. [**That's why I'm asking you to make a generous contribution to the Law Enforcement Legal Defense Fund (LELDF) today.**](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNTksInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAABBin67ab4jPFqKgvBdryt0fVnMVBg4A6f6pYOzXXkw0oDMUYkQDejtGDM3xKVtggtG9ZHZOis8-xnXGLI5tP5UVLlVDlyVB5nOa67v4) Brad has spent his entire adult life serving others. He's a proud Army combat veteran. A devoted husband and father. And for more than ten years, he served as a police officer with the Las Cruces Police Department. Then one afternoon everything changed. A robbery suspect attacked Brad's partner and knocked him to the pavement. During the struggle, the suspect gained control of the officer's taser and pointed it directly at him. In a matter of seconds, Brad was forced to make the decision no officer ever wants to make. He fired a single shot. His partner survived and went home to his wife and newborn baby. But our family's nightmare was only beginning. Because more than a year later, Attorney General Raul Torrez charged Brad with manslaughter. **To put New Mexico politics into context for you – Torrez is notoriously anti-cop and his campaign was bankrolled by leftist billionaire George Soros. ** _The same George Soros who, for the past decade, has spent tens of millions of dollars installing his hand-picked, police-hating puppets into prosecutors’ offices across America._ What followed was a trial filled with troubling questions and irregularities that ultimately resulted in Brad's conviction – **including a juror who failed to disclose their ties to Black Lives Matter.** Since the trial was overturned, Torrez and his junior Attorney General, R. John Duran II, have doubled down his desire to see my husband behind bars – and will use the full resources of the state government to finish the job. Now we're preparing for the next chapter of this fight. And we can't do it alone. **[That’s why I’m asking you to donate $25, $50, $100, or more to LELDF today.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNTksInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAABBin67acEAnUXa4koS9DKm16YQaLrO9G4mdXG7TEBZaWOfwVMTJ_X0gMJebrwO8xKZ2B1xqwrHsN1r8whH5S2KgunyDQwvIYyLmXM8s)** For over 30 years, LELDF has helped wrongly accused and convicted officers, like Brad, clear their names and win back their freedoms. From trials to appeals, and even presidential pardons, LELDF has a long track record of success. But they don’t receive taxpayer funding or grants, and large gifts are few and far between. Instead, LELDF relies on people like you who are sick and tired of progressive prosecutors trying to ruin the lives of good officers with bogus charges and witch-hunts. Brad’s first trial cost hundreds of thousands of dollars. With the games Torrez’s office is playing, we anticipate a second trial will cost even more. But your gift today ensures Brad receives the legal defense he deserves – not only at trial, but during this critical waiting period when Brad’s attorneys work to get the case dismissed. And believe me, they are working hard filing motions and investigating the corruption! [**So, can I count on you to make a generous, tax-deductible donation to LELDF today?**](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNTksInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAABBin67adTY_4mJxbGnWl0oIJLhidFkgg-XbplTSWgEg0UXD18QcSXcYFbCK_KhneuJWtPJfK3nR3UuIFIbmtiF7g54fn759Wyht5Fs0) Remember, the prosecution has unlimited taxpayer resources. Brad does not. Your gift today could be the difference between a strong defense and the next 11 years in prison. Thank you in advance for standing with my husband and backing the blue. Gratefully,
---
**_Lacy Lunsford_**
---
| | | [ **Support the Lunsford Family** ](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNTksInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAABBin67aeIetzKsgAlSyIMBsO2uWr3mYxsDrh6dBfBmXmzwk_xZCaQmPhjO--Ox8768kP1O8ykarHX6I2dNJ-dZ3cSnaDTGC9KtuiMBA)

name: Maya Stevenson
subject: These wins belong to you
body:
A short memo from the DNC’s Grassroots Cultivation Lead [ ](https://ak.democrats.org/go/98055?t=1&akid=10325%2E22930333%2E_lhslL)
---
Derek, this is Maya from the DNC Grassroots team. I’m reaching out today to _thank you so much_ for being on our team this year. **_Thank you_ for helping Democrats everywhere create such a historic blue wave this year.** This team helped us support _over 10,000_ Democratic campaigns with the organizing, tech, and data infrastructure they needed to compete up and down the ballot. As the Grassroots Cultivation Lead, it’s my job to connect with our Grassroots Partners who donate monthly to keep them informed about our work. But today, I wanted to reach out to _all_ of our supporters with an update about what we’ve accomplished this year. Whether you’ve chipped in once, twice, monthly, or if you’ve been supporting Democrats in other ways, every Democratic victory this year belongs to all of us, so this work should too. Here are some quick fun facts about our work and the perks of being a Grassroots Partner:
* 22.29% of all DNC grassroots fundraising comes from monthly donations.
* My team has hosted exclusive donor briefings for DNC sustainers and grassroots donors with Democrats like Elizabeth Warren, Roy Cooper, Mark Kelly, and Jamie Raskin to give our top supporters a true peek behind the curtain at where their support goes.
* When you become a Grassroots Partner, you receive only the most important updates from us. Your inbox and your phone won’t be overflowing with donation requests.

My team’s job is to make sure every donor feels fully in the loop about where their donation goes. **Our Grassroots Partners are the backbone of our work, and they are a key part of how we’ve been able to win up and down the ballot this year.** **If you’d like to become a Grassroots Partner to help the DNC in the fight to take back the White House in 2028, you can set up your monthly donation here:** [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-november-2026-gfr](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-november-2026-gfr?refcode=em_20261113_10325_dc&amount=7recurring=true) You’ll hear from us less, but when you do, we’ll be writing to show you _exactly_ what your monthly support is making possible. **[CONTRIBUTE](https://ak.democrats.org/go/99555?c0=em-dnc-november-2026-gfr.h1T69e&amount=7&refcode=em_20261113_10325_dc&t=6&akid=10325%2E22930333%2E_lhslL)** Thank you, The Democrats

_If you gave recently via check or mail, our system may not have yet processed your gift. We are appreciative and thank you greatly for your support._

Florida finally gets a taste of fall this weekend, with the season's coldest mornings arriving behind today's cold front. We've got all the details in today's Top Stories. Daytona Beach 🌤️ 73°/49° | Fort Myers 🌤️ 76°/55° | Jacksonville ☀️ 68°/42° | Key West 🌦️ 82°/70° | Miami 🌤️ 79°/59° | Ocala ☀️ 69°/42° | Orlando 🌤️ 74°/49° | Pensacola ☀️ 65°/38° | Port St. Lucie 🌦️ 76°/48° | Tallahassee ☀️ 67°/40° | Tampa 🌤️ 76°/50° | Florida Braces for Coldest Mornings Yet A strong cold front sweeping across Florida will deliver this weekend. Ocala could drop into the low 40s Saturday, while Orlando bottoms out in the upper 40s. The National Weather Service says there's a slim chance wind chills could briefly dip into the upper 30s near and north of Orlando. Farther north, the weather service says north of Interstate 10 tonight and Saturday night. Southwest Florida will wake up in the low to mid-50s , with isolated upper 40s possible in DeSoto County. Gusty north winds are expected to churn up rough water along the coast. The chill won't last: Central Florida highs climb back into the 70s Sunday, and rain returns to Southwest Florida early next week. Miami's Underline Trail Reaches 10 Miles Miami-Dade now has beneath the Metrorail tracks, running from Brickell to Dadeland. Organizers cut the ribbon Thursday on the completed Kenneth C. Griffin Urban Trail, a roughly $150 million project 12 years in the making and backed by federal, local, and private money. A bike crash led founder Meg Daly to envision the land under the rail line as a park and trail. She says Miami-Dade was among the nation's most dangerous places to walk and bike. The trail in May. The southern leg includes . A stewards program trains and pays people experiencing homelessness to maintain the grounds, and a few remaining parks should be finished by February. Teen's Match Fuels Big Bend Turkey Drive A Tallahassee 17-year-old will match every dollar donated to , up to $30,000, $5,000 more than last year. The money goes to Second Harvest of the Big Bend, which says each dollar covers up to four meals and that one in six area residents faces hunger. The drive aims to collect 1,000 frozen turkeys and $50,000 as grocery prices climb. Drop-offs are on Nov. 19 at Bannerman Crossing and Ponce de Leon Park, and meals go out on Nov. 21 at Governor's Square Mall. Elsewhere, a Jacksonville engineering firm is on Nov. 17-19 to feed more than 4,000 people, while Miami Gardens police instead of tickets to drivers stopped for minor infractions this week. | Flying together with our sponsor Unknown Number Calling? ## Tennessee SNAP Rolls Keep Shrinking
Tennessee's SNAP enrollment [continues to fall](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkLvO3CAQhZ8Gd1jMgG8FRRp3mzalxZphFwljCya29u0jp9gX-NuZc9F3_jyWh4sp5tdvt5FlDkumqyZiprLU7A7KZU9po8zBpVRPl_2nLqiwlwAS9OJWjictxjXePhEmZ9aGLAyT6foRlGne1rtuGgdPq--1mjo9BVB9p5H0qgOGsYn2DgQADaBGhJa8NqimATuD4whBGEU-8l5afhNTzlQrUUif_aTSrvvWJPtmPqrQvwTOAufrutrLMd1PgfNNJXD-Wu_T3-1JRe5B3pyy0BqPSJmrjFl-hdKX_ajSO3YC56ZYf1wxpVj7QRj12lxM__v5h-OdFv8FAAD__-vhhc8), with state data showing every county lost participants over the past year. About [609,500 Tennesseans received benefits in July](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFuhDAQheHTQLeI8RgwhYtI0XabNiUazLBYGgzCI9DePtrkCKnf01f834_hQVFien7Ryl51HhJfWViVjyEn2jkdm8jKSWcSySel6ZUHU5v2BnADHChoPHmwVE5-NNCTDSV76HrbtA5qWy6eRkRkChxGcISum3obHAK2hGNo2jL6NwgACFA7AxVPaE3dd6axxjmYC1vzFHU7Kl1YOSXOmXmW13byUYVtLcUvqnsu8KMw98Lcr-uqVl73JeZZXn-n94L3vcBP00DbN70rDz_tVxSJue0KWz9XivLr6T9jnN78BAAA__8Q9XLA), down 12.5% from nearly 697,000 a year earlier, after a federal law tightened work requirements and eligibility rules. Advocates with the Tennessee Justice Center say paperwork hurdles are causing some eligible people to lose benefits, while [federal officials dispute that eligible recipients are being removed](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OpDAQhJ_GZEbuxvwFDi4hm0svRB67GawzBtkt0Lz9ig12tfF22KUq1Vf_HvPDhhjS66_dyDAvc6KrRGKmPJdkD0p5j3GjxIuNsZw2-XeZUWEnASQ0s3UcTpq1rbx5IoxWu4oM9KNuuwGUrlZDT932nbK98-MTXavIely0c4vqxk5TFcwdCAANgBoQavKNRjX22GocBliEVuQD77nmlZhSolKIlvjeT8q127cqmpX5KKL5I3ASOF3XVV__c7pFgdNNJXD6sspjj4GD-_m8geU3sfR5P4rc9kySV5skqPsETnY7BE5VNv64QoyhdL3Q6rXZED_b8C-nPA1-BAAA___i7IqN). Starting this fiscal year, states also cover a larger share of SNAP's administrative costs, with the [federal share falling from 50% to 25%](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1urDAQxfGngW6RZ2y-ChdXutpu06ZEAx4vVoxB9gi0bx9tirxA6nP0K_6fj-lBIYb0_KCNrYifEl8lsgjnqSQ6OOU9xo2TeIqxnJTcq0yosLsB3EBPtEg4eTJUOzsjjGSWmi30o2m7AZSpV6up1XM7O29cT74FNA5nxcviR6Runutg3yAAaAA1IDTstEE19tgaHAbwlVHsguy5kZWFU-JSmH187SfnZtm3OtpV5CiV_lfhvcL7dV2NrCF9_b6bPT_fm74flf7fD6Ops3XHFWIMpesro54bhfijyR9TnBa_AwAA___qPHNT).
## Coldest Air of the Season Arrives
The [coldest air of the season](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJyk0LHOpCAUBeCnwQ7DveKoBcU2drPtloaR60iCYOCOxLffzCb7BH9zmpN8OTl_nsvT-uDj-7c9yDBvS6RaAjFTXkq0J8WcQjgo8mZDKJeN7i4LKnxIAAndYlf2Fy3aNs68ECar14YMDJPuHyMo3exGDYS0uX7o6NXRppzWdtKd7l1vp_XlGm--IAB0AGpEaMl1GtU0YK9xHGETWpHznHLLOzHFSKUQbeFOF-V2TUcTzM58FtH9EjgLnGutbS3H9S0Fzl9f4AzwP-4k7ySZjpOy5U-mIl2KLN_E8lPIyTUFJ-tOUXqWNmd_URE4N9m4s_oQfHkMQqv3YX34t4B_eN9l8G8AAAD__yyMhLc) settles over Tennessee through Sunday, and today should be the chilliest day, with highs in the 40s and wind chills in the 30s. A [widespread hard freeze is expected](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGurCAQxvGnwQ7DjCxiQXEbu73tLQ3KuJILaIDV7NufeIrzAqeZ5p_8Mvn-Paen9cGn118bydS6TomuEqhWylNJ9qCU9xAipbraEMppk_uUCQUqDsChm-xS_UmTtI0zM8Jg5dKQgX6QD6VByGYzvR3UPMt-1mqQHaw4S-dsr9yqHkJrary5QQDoAIRGaMl1EsXQ40Oi1rAyKcj5uue2blQpJSqFaA2f_aTcLntsgtlqPQrr_jAcGY7XdbVXiecdGY63z3AEuI-4u0-OH375X_j74NE7F4j_yDy-l40ve3CUufWZx_2kwnBssnHH5UPwRfVMile0Pnw_UH-53mnwKwAA__8MYYO9) Friday and Saturday nights, with lows in the 20s in many spots, the coldest temperatures since February. East Tennessee and the Smokies could see the [season's first snow showers or flurries](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkD3OpDAQRE9jMiN34-EncLAJ2Wy6ITLQHqwxZkS3sOb2KzbYC3xJJU96pao_z-npY4r59dvv5ETClKlwIhE6J87-Q_k8UtopS_Ap8eXz-uUJDbYaQEMz-UXiRZP11epmhMHbpSIH3WAfbQ_GVptr1gdSEwwC9kRLv9I8GNvZ1veznzuqoruFANAAmB6hprWxaIYOHxb7HoKyhtYox1nLRkI5EzNRSN_jorNejr1KbhP5sGp-KRwVjqWUuvB-3VDhePsVjgB3GIUj56Po_ybWIZ4sOiT_JtYlpqTvvVq2yLoQvRWO1enWz40it52y5rX7mP6Vyw-fuxz-DQAA__9qY4LD), while Johnson City may stay near 40 degrees through Saturday. Nashville will [likely see its first freeze of the season](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkL2uozAUhJ8GOpD_AFO42CZdtt0SneAhWDIG2WdBefsr8gq3HY1m9H3_ntOTQgzp_Zc2OOZlSrhKBDPyVBIdSHmPcUPihWIsJyX_KZMSqm-kbKSeaOZwYjJUe_dSciQz13ByGE3XWylMvTrttbG6txjQC5DpQWpWfTeMg9B21nVw96CUUksprJItvDZKjIPqjLJWLpUR8IH33PIKRkooBVjiZz-R23nf6uhW5qNU-k-lHpV6XNfV3ijzSikhdnfpjkG8IlfqkfYT2wu5kaL54rzCu2FsBzLx_4zG5_1oaAX5Ojt_XCHGUPqhMuK9UYjfV_6lstOpnwAAAP__786A8Q) this weekend, about two weeks past its Nov. 1 average, before highs rebound into the 60s next week.
## Crockett Statue Unveiled at Capitol
A bronze statue of frontiersman David Crockett, titled [_Guardian of the Frontier_ ,](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOszAQhJ_GdCB2McQULv6GLn97JdrYS2LFGGTvgfL2p5xO9wLXzmhmNN_Hdb5SiCHd_9PKVmSZE58lsgjnuSTaOeUtxpWTLBRjOSj5V5mxxaEGqKGbyUk4eNZUeXtDGEm7ii1cRt0PBlpdPSwSDHrpu8WjuRk0zK4dgMmP_Y2dHqtg34UA0AG0BqFh32lsxwv2Go2BRemWfZAtN_Jg4ZS4FOYlvraDc-O2tYr2IbIX1f1TOCmczvNszmdOb1Ph9H6lcPqN1j-Cp-NVu7y5J4vURUg-uZZUO9qDbFHhVGXr9zPEGMpwUbq9rxTi96T8kddh8SsAAP__wWOBmA) was unveiled Thursday at the Tennessee State Capitol. West Virginia sculptor Jamie Lester's design shows Crockett [standing atop a stone with his dogs, Rattler and Tigger](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFuhDAQheHTQLfIMx4bU7iIFG23aVMiLwyLJWMQHoG4fbTJEVK_p6_4vx_9I8QU8-srLOxFpj7zWRKL8N6XHDbO-5rSwlmmkFI5Qh6v0qNCewO4ge7DIPHgnkI9-idCF2io2UPbkbEOFNWzx1YDqnbQTyBlUDtiy86gbcmR7Vwd_RsEAA2gHELDoyZUXYuG0DmYKlI8Rln3RmYWzplLYZ7StR68N8O61MnPIlup9EeF9wrv53k2Cy_bHMuUrr_Te9H3rdKfaMBYA1TvftzOmFIstq1IvZYQ068n_4xxePwJAAD__2QrcOQ), in a strong frontiersman stance. The statue stands where a statue of newspaper editor and segregationist Edward Carmack [stood from 1927 until protesters toppled it in 2020](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFuhDAQheHTQLfIYxswhYtI0XabNiUy9nixNDYIj0B7-2iTI6R-T1_xfz_mh0uUyvPLZbTMcS54VUJmPOZa3I7l2IgyFo6OqJ6uhFedpZDDDeAGanae04mzdm2wi4TJad-ihXHS_WBA6Ha1kzMLYB-WpRcR_eS1UqPyXvTLYIxTbbJvEAAUgDASOgxKSzGNstfSGIiNFhgSb0fHKzKWgrUiRnptJx6d33JLdmXea6M-Gnlv5P26ri5j3tdUI73-Tu9F3fdGfcoeNEwA7WHDfiWiVIex0eKZXaJfj_8Z47TyJwAA__8P8HK0). Born in Greene County in 1786, Crockett [served in the Tennessee legislature and Congress](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OszAQAJ_GdEb4J_wULr6GLl97JVrshazO2MjeEOXtT5dXuHqk0Wi-7ssdKFLa_8OBjnlbEr5qRGYsS01wYio5xgMTbxBjvSCFd110p3uplFRmAc904WKhCW7VagLrG3RqmOytH1Vnm4czZsXJw9Rbb6Zh7a0JXt0s9EFt_TasDblfoVLKKNWNWrUYjNXdNOib1eOoNmE7DMS5tPxAxpSwVsQtvvOFpfX5aKJ7MJ9VmH9Cz0LPnKBw9fk4qFbKqc1lF3q-qD4hyg8rsPGBgUAGrLQnoecAFwXpS_bfyCzXZ2X5TBdSxCA5ycrAKD2cxDkKPTfFhfNFMVLtB2G7_QCKnx7-48zL6Z8AAAD__9sIjXM) before dying at the Alamo in 1836.

It 's Not Random** The BBC caught scam call center workers on hidden cameras as they laughed at the people they were tricking. One worker bragged about making $250k from victims. The disturbing truth? Scammers don't pick phone numbers at random. Hey everyone. With this new Congress, I think we have a responsibility as Democrats and as Americans to figure out what we actually want from the people we send to Washington.
_For just $5 a month, you can subscribe to The Angry Democrat and help support my work. I 'd really appreciate your support!_
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..PFhkQAsvV9lsGrH4xOTIPHx3foaX-T2EzTKI7CVGe3U?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=224676453)
I gave you my list last time: healthcare for all, a balanced budget, less debt, and getting corruption out of Congress. No more stock trading. Overturn Citizens United. Today I want to start with healthcare, because it's easy to say everybody should have it. What does that actually look like?
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/74cf2e4f-5680-4083-8078-d750ce685769?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I've talked with [Abdul El-Sayed](https://open.substack.com/users/25053904-abdul-el-sayed?utm_source=mentions) in the past, and he's been laser focused on getting healthcare to everybody. He's helping lead that conversation. But even among people who agree on the goal, we still have to answer some pretty basic questions.
Who pays?
Who runs the hospitals?
What happens to the insurance you already have?
And what do you owe when you go to the doctor?
Over the next few months, as this Congress gets to work, we're going to look at how other countries answer those questions and what, if anything, might work here.
Maybe some versions are within reach and others aren't. To be perfectly honest, I don't think we've had an honest conversation about what we'd be paying for, what we'd be giving up, or what we'd get in return.
So let's start there.
Healthcare for all is a goal. To understand any plan, ask three questions:
Who is covered, and for what?
Who puts in the money and who pays the bill?
Who owns the hospital or runs the practice?
Then ask what happens when you walk in the door: Can you get an appointment, and what will you owe?

The _SS United States_ , a record-setting ocean liner [_built at Newport News Shipbuilding_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkL2unDAQhZ8GOiNszI8LF2nobtqUaNaMYbTGRngWtG8fsUmk9LeY6jsanfP9-pq-gALF5SdsaPn0U8QrB2TGYzrpWCgSkEsxv-LzCQFWOChNqladkFLIZgLHdOKkoZytB41gSrSyN7rtBl3rcrVGK3TSo4f50ULnezeY3tQwNKZ79EaWZO9_Usrmc6bS2Le1d67umqE3Q1voGmfidFS84r9WPrzTiUfl0lYGuzLvuWh-FGos1HhdV3Xx8wMLNd6bCjVSFLyicGnbXpH4_Yfs6WDxN5GzuAnOIjMwZvE_FwEXcG8R6MQsUhSQhYftDq-0C8rillQedt4vCoFy1xe6Xjag8CnJ3_R7WvU7AAD__3mRk_c) and delivered in 1952, was sunk off the Florida coast on Wednesday to become the world’s largest artificial reef. Crews flooded the 990-foot ship in a [_controlled, explosive-free sinking_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u5CAMhZ8m6RgBIX8FxTbp7rZbRh5iEmsIXIE3aN9-ldHOE2xhS7aP7OPv19f6BRQo7j_hRMuXXyPWEpAZ83pR3ikSkEux_I6vFwQ4IFNatdSDUEqobgXHdOFqoN2sB4Mwt2jVOJt-mIw07WFB4Sinbpj1DINzw-R7lGqcn_j0pn-OLdl7n1Kqe8f8MDj20jsnh24a56lvjMSNOOUHH_hx5cOfdGF-uHS2wR7M36XpfjR6afRSa33UEso9bPRy_3R3kfIm_hX3yUYvSn0SH1REcghRBIqYRYUi-EBRUw5bER4KY2FBXMQTKe7iZiI4iRNe-FYGyPstgczkyREEkRF9o5c22-27UghUhrExcj-Bwts6_yf1y-q_AQAA___FVZh1) about 25 miles southwest of Destin-Fort Walton Beach, and the ship settled in 180 feet of water. Longer than the _Titanic_ , it surpasses the carrier _USS Oriskany_ as the largest vessel ever sunk as a reef. The liner set a transatlantic speed record on its maiden voyage that still stands, carrying passengers from Hollywood stars to a young Bill Clinton before it was mothballed in 1969. The $13.5 million project aims to draw divers and anglers. Some 3,000 workers built her [_in Hampton Roads_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkDHO4yAUhE-DOyyMCY4Lim3cZdstrRd42E_BEAHByu1XifSf4C9GU4w0-mb-3dYbUKC4_YUDTW1-jXiWgLViXhvljSIB2RTLKz4eEGCHTGmVQmo-DHwYV7CVGq4KOmc8KIS5QzNMs7roqxKq241zd6knlGIcvQYLVs_3CdGNep6kULIj8-kbhmH8au4VThfhrRV6vE7z9cKUQEc15b7u-EPlwzs1zL1NRxfMXuuzsPEPkwuTy3me_Qnt_QmZXBo5TEwupfBXpIqOlwoVC_-s4sl77kPK5IDbBKXygNAobjxAqV_HDeybU-Q7HM-aIs8JXGFy6bJxz5NCoKInpsR2AIUvUv3lm83I_wEAAP__Hp2NEQ) in 1950 and 1951. Pieces of the liner remain in Newport News: her bell at Christopher Newport University and a 34-ton propeller at The Mariners’ Museum.

## Lawmakers Rethink Killer Outing Privileges
Virginia state [_Sens. Dave Marsden and Scott Surovell_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO5CAMhp-GdIyAYZJQUFyTbq-9MvISk1ghEAGbaN_-xErzBFvYjX___vz_-5g_gALF9S8caOvl54h3CVgr5vmivFIkIJdi-Yr7DgE2yJRmJVTPpeTyOYOrdOGsoVusB41gOrRyMPrVj1robrOjEeJzMBLN5yj9CwDQuaWNvUEYZEe2-Ukpnz9lHhqHl_DOif45DmZ8MS1woZryo274pvLhO12YHy4dXbBbrWdhzz9MTUxN930_zlTTAS4kB6GJmJraGaYmKVsTTE1vLx7gPmDHXHj7lRbM3G0QV4orzxgQCjZN4eArZr5TCJi5D4ht4yvW_M1T5CeUwtTUZbucN4VApR-YFusB9MPQ1V9mfFn1PwAA__9uKZN0), both Fairfax Democrats, are weighing changes to a law that lets the state behavioral health commissioner grant unescorted community outings to some violent patients, even over a judge’s objection. People found not guilty by reason of insanity go into the custody of the Department of Behavioral Health and Developmental Services rather than prison, even in killings. A judge must approve a conditional release, but not unescorted outings of up to 48 hours. The push follows the case of Abdulloi Toshpulodzoda, found not guilty by reason of insanity in his landlord’s 2019 killing. Toshpulodzoda [_fled to Tajikistan_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOqzAQRb8GOiNsbIgLF6-hy2u3RLNmDKMYO7INbP5-RaR8wRZTjc7VuffrPt2BPIXlP2xoyuGmgGf2WAqm6aC0UCAgG0Pew-MBHlZIFCfRip5xzng3gS104CShno0DiaBrNHzQUvU32cp6NZpbCV07aACwCApFpxT0TvXdt9ZS1mSuPM559z7dSBxU66xt--426JuqZIszlZiasuLHyvlXPDA1Nm61N2spz1x1_yoxVmI8z7Nx8UfN9npXYrxaVWL8sGy50BATe6a4UcbM7AphQQauYGJg7Z5xZtueZkyYmPOIme0sM5fixjYMBTxbEXxZmQNLnsqrTmZ-nuQ95X6oZLtsQP7tV_447WHEbwAAAP__fTySVQ) in July on an unescorted pass. Longer than the Titanic , it surpasses the carrier USS Oriskany as the largest vessel ever sunk as a reef. ## Nvidia CEO Huang Resigns amid Scandal
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang [resigned Thursday](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDHO4yAUhE-DOyy_h2PigiKrlbVNttliS4vAwybCEAGxlduvvP8R_nI0mtHM9_c-37UPPi6_9UaqujRHOkqgWinPcffWa0OpCO2c9rk4suZdy4wdDhyAg5i1qX6nGRqrHBGSaEiBHPvLMPa9bFb1GLvxakiCgAdaMFekEUYki3gxHZjGq7MOAASA6PDa0kNIbbW8CEcgxcD6jqyvKbfP5GNdyYVP2im3Jm1NUGutr8LEjeHEcDqOo91KPD2GE0X-LgynLUX6MJwqmTWmkJZTfP3jhhJ_UiwU-frWceGZil_iGdOZ3264Oml_MTEl4y0TP3-cuOgofyi_mqzs6_Ah-DJI1nfLpn34v6t-j-au8F8AAAD__5OAibI), effective immediately, after reports of two extramarital affairs, one with a senior Nvidia executive and one with an executive at a Singapore data firm whom U.S. intelligence officials suspect of working for China. Hours later, Reuters reported that he also had a relationship with a [second Nvidia employee](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLHSmzAQhJ8GuvMgCSxTqEhD96dNyZylE1wsJEYSEL99xkneIO3Ozs5-34-v-Qs5cFy-40am-jRHukqgWinP8WTHaCkVhd4j5-LJ2aOWWXbyDkKAUDPayifNonXGE0lSLRmhx364j32v29W4h7Tq6UXvHg_3VN3ohBhGh27UNGoxtGw-c0IIJYTq5ONGT6XRoR6UJ6HVvek7clxTvv1MHOtKPrzTSflm09YGs9a6l0Z9a-TUyOm6rhvHk0rluHwajZw-TI2cSk32BRvmF1X4l9EvG47CJ_mUN8rwlxksJVgPjAus6AAhU8DKKZaVd7i4roBQyKbogLY9pDcRlHRkSwUKvmHopOpU32bj9otD4HLXTd8tG3L4c7v-n-zTyN8BAAD__wcFl0c), citing two people familiar with the matter. ## Killeen ISD to Close for Hasan Execution
Killeen ISD will [close all schools and facilities](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykULGu2zAQ-xp5U6A7y3E8eOji7XXtaFyk07MQRQqki53-feH-wgMHEiBAkPzztX5RTDF__6Ynz_IJZc18tMQiXNfmKh9HqU9HjVt7xQdTk1raigavGkBDv5KTuPMKnZ_vxk_Q8QzjZIcRcBq6be69uVofnOc-BPSDw2m8G2-tG30frtzF-UwDgB7QQI-XOxgLMFlv-UaDB2UN-yilXmRj4Q-1kP6WnevFlWeX5k3k1VT_S-GicDmO4_JwnGU_bYULVYkuscLlnKZwScVRUrg8YkrMWcfmdXNbKUm7VNq7ctMbNcqaP-zeEkvWmU6ipEmE86kVLoMx2vJ0wug7Ba8thZu-kWGN_c2ZASdAx12d_euIKcV2HZU130-K6X95-eHn-4z_AgAA__8fbZfO) on Thursday, Dec. 3, the day Nidal Hasan is scheduled to die by firing squad at Fort Hood for the 2009 shooting that killed 13 people. District leaders called the closure a safety step ahead of expected traffic and national media attention. Killeen police reportedly recommended the shutdown. The district plans to limit [after-school activities](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL3u4yAQxJ_G7rDYBX8VFNe4y7VXWhtYxyjYRMCF5O1Pvlf4N6ORRprR_P7c1hv54M_HbzrYlM8W15NrDlwKpzXbxLXGdFjKnPPLP5lySTGvKHEQAALUSrb4N6_QOnOXboaWDYyz7kfAuW93M7NSaO3AA0rWk6VpknfathEU91ph683VBgAKUILC7g5SA8zaaZ6od9Boyc6XmLqyc-EP5S1845tTZ-PRBrOX8sqN-tXg0uBSa-2-tMd4pQ0u158Gl7-XUCreBr7s02cnbIiZhaOvOL2jIHbKdAoYcO71MKluL0dok3Gv6kPweRgbLR8H-fB_ufwQ2NvgvwAAAP__WQ6ABA) that day to UIL competitions and varsity practices. Hasan, a former Army psychiatrist, admitted to the attack and was sentenced to death in 2013. If carried out, it would be the [first military execution since 1961](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDGOpDAQRU8DmVsuY2AIHGxCNptuiDx2eSi1wS1XdZu9_ar3CpN_fb33_nxun54ynd-__YFOrlS2ExtnFMG6cajYWqlH8IzMD7qjZ6mFN6PNpAAUDJsPQi_coI_uS8cFenQwL3acwSxjv7sZ9YyjH_w0LdbEpJcwJvsBc7KTn9LYk3u_AcAARsNgbl-gLcBio8UPP0borMZIUupNdhS8PKf8t7yw3kI5-ux2kQd3w6_OrJ1ZW2u3VK7ZP1nofE86s76lOrPeKWfEUxFHFYmlUpBGEVXIhZ8V1UnRZ7V79qfCC8NTqJwqlSpqLyUq3ksRrH118dEoZ-Jp7qz-Pjzl_zTyw4gvZ_4FAAD__1_iisk), though Hasan could still seek a delay in federal court.
## Screwworm Cases Spike as Weather Cools
[Confirmed cases](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOnDAQxvGnMZ2Rx4ZdKFxEiugubUo0a88u1hmMPAPcvX2UFPsC6b7q01-_3x_zB6acttcvXMnL17PMG12cSYTqzKHSdZW6BmRi3tMnIUstPFtjbxpAg5sxSDpphib6h4kjNOThPnb9HezYN4s3vXs658ZhGIyxsYeB8BYwdDfT9_b-aJL_-wYADqwBZ9sHmA5g7GJHA_YRVGcoJim1lYWEvpCf-bucVNtQ1ib7RWRn5X4oOyk7XdfV4r4kbg-O2L7KqeyEW1ox83vphTDLouyU00ksJXxq3KLey5GlfuuYmJBJ2Yml7PoNoewUjlppE82CcrBy044vUu4nNNXH_Uo5J77dVWdeK6b8L1H-U_b09k8AAAD__4ZWkEo) of the flesh-eating New World screwworm in Texas, New Mexico, and Arizona [have reached 128](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2SnTAQhE8DmShG_AcKnJCtU4fUIA2LygJRmtkn7NO7HoEvsPlX3f31r4_lA33w5-dPPMjIvcXlpMyBRCgtbBPlHNNhkYn58r8JWVLkRde6VwAKmgWt-BctUDqz1m6CkgwMU9sNoKeu3E2zNt3Y9Nvo0JIbcBundnXUWRgHGKat9OadBgAN6BoaXa1QtwBT61oasXNQtDU5LzFVspPQjbyFP_FFqbLxKIPZRS4umh-Fngs955yrLd663-MXSzzfUKHnt1ah5y92qBJdMQkr3jFd6vFSJ2WVYwpO_bdW_tyIBcXHkxXaFJnV0__QB93eRoXJ_40nlsm4K_sQPPdD0dafB_rwDJRv_voy-l8AAAD__-wVku4), with 42 new livestock and pet infestations in the first 11 days of November alone. Officials logged just seven domestic cases across August and September before the October count jumped to 36. A Texas A&M insect specialist said summer heat [held the flies back](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLFugzAURb_GbEa8hwkweOjClq4dkbEfiRWDkf0Sp39f0aE_0OUuVzpX93xd56vxwe-3T7OR5vca551KDsRMac42USkxbdZkyvnwDzKZU8wzNniRABLa2Vj2L5qhcnpp3AgVaehH1fWAY1fdtWnHdrGLbXo34NB2w2Uha93qbG-HQbnK65MGAC1gAy3WCzQKYFRO0WA6B0I15DzHVPOdmN4mr-E7vijVNm5V0HfmI4v2Q-AkcCql1I-F32cpcDrZAieAM1DgdEvxuTv5PGTymeRORZaYgpN_b6XfV8ps2Mc9C5yqpN1RfAg-X3qhmttmfPjd5n8qe2n8CQAA___NroGO), and cooler days in the 70s and 80s have allowed numbers to climb. Officials are enforcing limits on animal movement and operating checkpoints in parts of 21 Texas counties. The Agriculture Department is also [hiring 228 workers](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGunDAQRb8GOq8YY-BRuEhD99KmRIM9hlGMvbIny9u_j3YV5QdeO3N179H59bl-IkdO-088ycpXyGuiq0YSobJWV-i6cjkdVqr1zr8Jq5RcV93pUQEo6Fd0wg9aofV26_wMLVmYZjNMoOehPSxhgDDoDz1607tAQUOYhg7H2QOOw9iyfbUBQA-6g17fNugMwGy8oQ8cPDSmI8-Sy00OEvrCGuIzP6jcXD7baA-Re236H41eGr28-E3FhEly4vzK_Ls2eonZYWz08qd6VBvtnKo6uHDaVchFJbrUe0AFdBxZnkqycvncUN7PK5fo1X8vbbH-fnGMXMepMd1-Isc3lXxT5sPqvwEAAP__zDeNgQ) for an Edinburg plant set to produce 100 million sterile flies a week in 2027, so wild females lay eggs that never hatch.
## SpaceX Eyes First Double Starship Catch
SpaceX will attempt to catch both stages of its 407-foot Starship rocket this weekend as they return to Starbase, a feat that would make it the [first fully recovered orbital rocket](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDGOpDAQRU9jMiOXMQ0EDjYh6003RAUuwFqDkV0NPbcf0ckcYOL3VKr3_z2HJ_rg9-UvbmT5PcdhpysHYqY05CnRdcW0TZgp58P_J8ycYh600g8JIKEacGJ_0gCFs6NyHRRkoelM3YDu6mK1ncJZt2DGtibd1KatWuiwalrXaVTOFd7e1wCgAq2g0uUIygB0xhlqsXYgjCLnOaaSV2J6Y57DVzwplVPcimBX5iOL6o_QvdD9dV1lPnCimwrd3z1C98GfJHT_IW-ZGVNe_SHn4JeVJdTyFuTrcMiU5R7PO--T-eP6lFm6-BoDyYC78_sikZm2g4tk3XH5EHx-NMKoZUMfPv_xL2c9rf4OAAD__4F7jr8) in history. Liftoff is [set for 4:45 p.m. CST](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LHOozAQBOCngc4RawyEwsU1dLn2SmTsJazOYOTdQPL2v8gr_P2nmdH8e4wPR5G251-3opX3nMYNT44ognlkn_E8U169Y2Te6T86lpx41JVuFYCCenRe6MARymCnKvRQooWuN00Hum_Kxc6-7XznXVcjBm1aj05PDYC_183dG12SvdIAoAZdQa1vE1QGoDfB4N01AQpTYSBJ-SYLCr4dz_GTDsw3n9Yy2kVk56L-U-ih0MMXTCkHzNOLaUPmyxV64N15fCsWl3mhXc2RnosoaJQgC6uVmCltak5Zza8Y1YEL-Ygqo7_qPirgmjaW7ORyWzoU1LIUeiizDftJMRK3XWGq5-oofufJL189rP4JAAD__57CkWE) from the company's second launch pad in Cameron County. About six minutes later, the launch tower's mechanical "chopsticks" will try to pluck the returning Super Heavy booster out of the air. ## Data Centers Divide Dems
Data centers could test state Democrats' incoming trifecta, with party leaders [split](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJyk0D1u6zAQBODTSB0F8U-0ChavcefXphTWy7VFgBQNci3BPn3gIDdIPcA3g_m6LBeIKW73_5DJM7xvy0ZHS8RMdQmUQ9xjoLaWnWqlTPlKlcKiRjUJKYXUCyDHnRYDffB6wtmZnrx0s7HOmtH1q59wtjBbM-N4AntzbnKaLElS2kgtpz76jyel1FKP1pphdKhPAdSMiGTBdGakELnUgVeCGt9lg1t6fUYNWHKf_Mr8aJ3-16lzp87HcQxwRWk_aafOazlEAAaBtDHVJrA8UxBMjcUvJwLlghW4iecW-dVXHx5HTCm2yXVmvGeI6aeM__rT7tV3AAAA__9zon6a) over a statewide moratorium on projects. Meanwhile, SpaceX [released](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJykkL8O2yAQh58Gb0T8NcnA0MVbuna0MFzik8C24OKkefqKqm_Q5ZZP9-nT79d9vgfMuD1_hgKewvcxb_BuGYigzglKwhMTtHU_oVYoUBaokGYl1Mil5FLPIRKeMJswJK_HeHNmAC_dzVhnjXDD6qO9OiUgaDsKLfRiUxqvS3SLEaOTRg7ou09KqaUW1pqLcFFfU1C3GCPYYJgRkJD2eqEVQsXvvoVH_t2jLnEvQ_Yr0dGY_sHUxNT0pnMJpSOmpu5mapKyH8XU1I4Q4cNp57id0Ih3D3eGL5gz7hvHjbfXATXu5XgR8EeImJEQWkcEn9D4vwqmpqH6dLz7axsdM-JZAua_WfS_i55e_QkAAP__0R2LVQ) more details of its planned $50 billion data center campus in Cochise County, promising about 1,000 permanent jobs. Among Democrats, Gov. Katie Hobbs opposes a moratorium while state Attorney General Kris Mayes [backs](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJyk0D3unDAQQPHTmM7IXyxL4SIN3T9tSjTYAzixMbJHIDh9tFFyglzg6af342v6ghDDvn6HhJbgWaYdrxqRCMvkMflwBo91yyeWggnTjAX9pIR6cSm51BM4CidOBhpv9csNvWnQyn4wXd8Z0TebNbMS3jjltesGPb_dYhbwWkn_FvKt5ibYT09KqaUWXWda0Tv99qAG5xx2YJgR6APl0tKGUMKTd1ji_UG1Lqcm2o3oqEx_Y2pkaryuq_3183naXFamRozoKOS9MjX-k4sXUyPsKxb-yXDcsaw3d7lS5R4IuMOdsFSe4OYbnMiPkg-MET2veGKByP9SuMeUXQGqnDI_g6Nc7qZYf1whxlBfPTNiTRDiHy397-jTqt8BAAD__-vXlmI) one and incoming Senate President Priya Sundareshan said the idea should be considered. Some Democrat leaders also want to extend the suspension of data center tax breaks beyond a three-year pause state lawmakers approved in June. Developers rushed to submit applications before the pause took effect July 1.
## Mattel Theme Park Faces Uncertainty
The planned Mattel Adventure Park in Glendale [remains](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJykkL3OozAQRZ_GdCD_YihcbEOXbbdEE88kWGsDMhNQ8vSr7Ct89ZXuOTp_bvMNUk7r8zcUCgyfx7zSdWRipjojFUxnQjqW7aRaqVC5UyWctdR9q1SrzAyR00mzhQaD6ePobUNB-dE676z0zRKsl4MZyfTSDeC8BAmDQkAdnRpif29S-P4ppYwy0jnbSR_NgKDHGCM5sMJKwsRb7XghqOmzrfDI769UF7fS5LAw74cwv4SehJ6u6-qOxxOYvrPQE6ZjpXeGFYWeoHKKmYSeCjBTbgFPWvlVqd2h_m1fOwJTq7WTo9Wu25e9qQH3K-Wcjt4LK58FUv6P5p9WO4P-FwAA__9Qm4KJ) unfinished, with no opening date announced following years of delays. Park developer VAI Resort [said](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOozAYBOCnMZ0jbEwIhYtr6PbaK9Efe0is_cGR-dfc5ulP3CtsPdLom_nzMX9Q4rQ9ftMKL_Re5g3HzhBBmSPWmGqK2J-5ohSsWO8oiLNt7VUbo003U5BUMTtqou-uYRxcA2-G0fVD79qhefrO2CE6R4QRY2tvi7H99b6QRRvMzd6b5M8-Y0xnurbv3aUdQneLZMcQAnpyyrWISXK5yBNU0jtvtPD3ibqEvDbsnyKvXXW_lJ2UnY7juNA9mP5MlZ3OTcpOBY-UN31gF12JGd_KTg_GFomh7FQp6YI9F9FCn9j18sWsQ96kZNZ50SuJgDXFik2-CvSLyqemRVB0RAXnF4rG3yRN8fF1JOa0Xwfl2sdKif9b5ac3V2__BQAA__86fpZj) in August that an announcement on the project's status could come this month. The park, first slated for 2023, has been delayed several times, and the adjacent billion-dollar VAI Resort also appears [unlikely](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJyk0LHOpCAUBeCnwQ4DiDIWFNvYzbZbmjtw1ZtFMEA0ztNv3Ff4-5Nzvpw_7_kNFCiuv2FHW-G7zBGvErBWzLPH3dNJHsuWTswZd9w_mNHPSqiBS8llN4OrdOKsofG2G9xodINWmlH3ptfCNJtdOhgXqbxGOfSv3i0fP7rRII6Dw5fxDdmnT0rZyU70vW6Fcd3Lgxqdc9iDZlqgp5pyWzeETN8UYQn3g2pd2ptgt1qPwrpfTE1MTdd1tfBdYKdwPwGmpmeBqUlopiYpmJpOIJ6xpFz5GjB6CMgD_cVw85gqTwdGiiuvGxV-I2QOS8XMPYIPFJEfUAoWpqYmW39cFAKVwTAt1h0o_GfVnz56WvUvAAD__5aujNk) to open this year. The developer envisions Hot Wheels-themed roller coasters, Barbie-themed attractions, and more than 2,500 jobs at the park. VAI took over as developer, owner, and operator this summer after Epic Resort Destinations [stepped](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJykkL2uozAUhJ8GOkfYGAyFi23osu2W6GAPwRvzI_uE7ObprxLdN7j1jGY-fX-u45VCDNvtN62wTK953PDMEcxIo8fqwxk88rKfSAkr1gkJflSVaoWUQtYjOQ4nRk2lt3XreqNLWGl63ZhGV6ZcrJo67U1PHdzUdA1a1Zq2qzzJGcbMdRnse09KWcu6ahp9qYyrO0-qd86hIV3oCj7wni68gFJ47RvN8f8b6uL2tYx2YT5yUf8q1FCo4c70CQo1fLfF9MhhQ86FGlZiRhTkT2z8SBAHpbvwOBH3A0ngX-AsjrT_heMyWX88Q4wht6bQ1W2lED-n_FNfp1VfAQAA__-0MIMQ) away from the project.

You can find more information about the post [here](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJyk0LtqwzAUxvGnkbcYXX0ZNGTx1JRuhS7iRDqOD5WsIAub5umL-wrdP358_D9v7gYUaX28Q0Jb4TW7FY8tYq1YXMAUaKeA25J3LAUTpjsWDE5y2V2EuAjlwFfa0WloglWdH3vdoBX9qE1vNO-bxXIwA_edVxzHYR641GacO8k7HdCP3DRkT08IoYTixuiW914NAeTovUcDmmmOgWoubV0QCr3yCnP8OU-1Pqcm2qXW58bUlcmJyek4jnYGj_ecv88Bk9M1YSEP6xs-KK8feataXb-YnJpiw_OgGGnreqb5IwHFP7X-N8hu5W8AAAD__z-odVQ). The virtual legion post is among several newer initiatives aimed at helping veterans across the state, including a nonprofit's [ongoing construction](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJykkDvOpDAQhE9jMo_84hU42ITs33RD1NgNtGQbZFuwM6dfMVfYpJMuVX1Vf37mH6BAafsNEW2FzzonvEvAWjHPHqOnizyW_bgwZ4wYF8zoZyVUx6XkUs_gKl04G2i81Z0be9Oglf1o2r41om92u3iN4zhAOwyDcEZ0i9FGLdqtnevXTjZkHz8ppZZatK15id7pwYManXPYgmFGoKd65FfdETJ9jgRreD9QL3fEJti91rMw_Yupianpvu8XfFaIFN6PgKnpSWBqkvI5iqlpC5g8BOQXhQAb8jMfT1feCl4pvfl-RCz8wooZUuH498RMmByl7fsLWErCUpiammz9eVMIVLqeGbFFoPAlq_876mXVvwAAAP__WqCNZQ) of 50 tiny homes in Glendale for veterans experiencing homelessness.

It 's Not Random** The BBC caught scam call center workers on hidden cameras as they laughed at the people they were tricking. One worker bragged about making $250k from victims. The disturbing truth? Scammers don't pick phone numbers at random. Hello Friend, Spiritual strength doesn't come in a single moment. It's built over time. And after more than 40 years of pastoring and preaching God's Word, I've learned that consistent time in Scripture is the key to a grounded, courageous life of faith. That's why I created the brand-new _**[2027 Pathway to Victory Daily Devotional](https://email.editor.goppresidential.com/c/eJyc0cGO2yAQBuCnwTdbhrGhOXBo5bqnbbenPaIJTAgSNghjV3n7Kmmi3vc8_z-aT_PxZt4wxLD6n7iQ9ilnUzaDDkO8OTpSDWnFWNOVYr6l3YheyJbzloNBW8NBZsDG6QHlIKVsSHN1GkY1KiGbq1ZqUCCAOInLSUHvlEWF7oIwOgQJTdD3hZxz4MBH0XecHLcOTlKOX-hMZzb05EJNpbvfVmgLjtYaMHY2LU3U11rzxuArEzMT80Z2L9TlenSpeCZm0QvV5no413rPGcxb2oslY5MjBtPH929MyL0uxuKSMfiVwfSwm__4Z-Jfk8GUS9oy2RpW_xwt5MK-MJhowfDK27RWWiuD6bdqf_x6f29f1KZol_-EGMMmFRt6f289PPWzHzi0-BsAAP__KVOYAQ),**_ a weekday guide to help you start each day with biblical truth and encouragement. Every devotional in this 260-entry collection was written to help you think biblically, live obediently, and trust God more fully. Whether you're struggling with uncertainty, carrying the weight of past mistakes, or simply seeking God's direction, this resource is designed to meet you right where you are. You'll begin the year by discovering how to embrace the new beginning God offers. You'll turn your attention to Jesus Christ through Holy Week and a study of the end times. You'll follow the early church and see how the Holy Spirit empowered believers to stand firm in their faith. And you'll close the year examining the attitudes that shape your life, learning to find contentment and experiencing the freedom of forgiveness. These are not abstract ideas. They are time-tested truths drawn from over four decades of biblical teaching to help you walk closely with Christ each day. This beautifully produced 532-page devotional features a velvet red leather cover, rich gold and brown foil accents, and larger, easy-to-read print, making it both a meaningful spiritual investment and a joy to use.

Team,
I have a message for the health insurance companies, big tech companies, defense contractors, big oil, and billionaires who think they can buy influence in Washington:
**I am not your friend. I can’t be bought. Don’t try.**
This congressional seat belongs to the people. And that’s who I’ll answer to in Washington.
When I was a kid, I watched my mom spend years fighting our insurance company to get the care she needed. That experience helped drive me to become a lawyer and run for office.
I’m taking that experience with me to Congress, and my commitment to fight for Medicare for All.
The people who helped us win deserve someone who will keep fighting for what we promised. People who need care deserve someone willing to stand up to the companies getting in their way.
**Team, your support helped make this victory possible. But the real work starts now. **

# ReproMatters

---|---
| Peter —

This month’s midterm elections in the United States made clear what we have long known: **the great majority of Americans support reproductive rights**. Voters approved state measures to protect abortion rights, rejected an anti-abortion measure, and elected the most pro-reproductive rights Congress in history.

From protecting access to critical healthcare, including abortion and miscarriage care, to reaffirming our right to control our own bodies and lives, the incoming members of Congress have committed to protecting all of our rights. What’s more, new leadership in states across the country – including Texas and Georgia, which have long been anti-rights strongholds – offers the promise of dramatic, positive change.

**We are prepared and eager to do the hard work to ensure that we make the most of these historic opportunities. **We are already partnering with newly elected champions of reproductive rights and will provide ongoing guidance. Key priorities include:
* Building new momentum to pass the Women’s Health Protection Act, federal legislation that would protect abortion rights and access nationwide
* Pushing for removal of harmful provisions in the “One Big Beautiful Bill” that stripped away Medicaid coverage for essential healthcare
* Working with Congress to advance bills to expand access to maternal healthcare, contraception, and IVF
* Fighting in the courts to preserve reproductive rights in states where anti-rights extremists continue to attempt to restrict access to reproductive healthcare

As always, the [Center’s website](https://click.everyaction.com/k/143387551/660045930/1485890129?sourceid=1151712&utm_campaign=27emgus-1101aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=repromatters&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlOTllODUyMi02ZmRmLWYxMTEtOTFmMC0wMDBkM2ExOGUyNDQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=xtvahfuwo84pmVnfvKBQnHCqhBAUxk1AdTj0VY3dOtY=&emci=2fe8f888-a3d4-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&emdi=e99e8522-6fdf-f111-91f0-000d3a18e244&ceid=954237) offers a wealth of resources. clean_body: Eying a promise of dramatic change. | | | | | ReproMatters ---|--- | Peter — This month’s midterm elections in the United States made clear what we have long known: the great majority of Americans support reproductive rights. Voters approved state measures to protect abortion rights, rejected an anti-abortion measure, and elected the most pro-reproductive rights Congress in history. From protecting access to critical healthcare, including abortion and miscarriage care, to reaffirming our right to control our own bodies and lives, the incoming members of Congress have committed to protecting all of our rights. What’s more, new leadership in states across the country – including Texas and Georgia, which have long been anti-rights strongholds – offers the promise of dramatic, positive change. We are prepared and eager to do the hard work to ensure that we make the most of these historic opportunities. We are already partnering with newly elected champions of reproductive rights and will provide ongoing guidance. Key priorities include: Building new momentum to pass the Women’s Health Protection Act, federal legislation that would protect abortion rights and access nationwide Pushing for removal of harmful provisions in the “One Big Beautiful Bill” that stripped away Medicaid coverage for essential healthcare Working with Congress to advance bills to expand access to maternal healthcare, contraception, and IVF Fighting in the courts to preserve reproductive rights in states where anti-rights extremists continue to attempt to restrict access to reproductive healthcare As always, the offers a wealth of resources. You may be especially interested in , our up-to-the-minute tool showcasing abortion laws in each U.S. state; our , a one-stop shop for everything you need to know about ongoing threats to abortion pill access; and , a tool that tracks Trump administration actions and appointees who pose a threat to reproductive rights. | | Peter, Today is deadline day in Alaska — it’s the final day for absentee ballots mailed within the U.S. to arrive and be counted. **Alaska is officially the last statewide race of the midterms left to be called.** Every other Senate race in America has been called — Democrats will hold at least 55 seats. Mary Peltola's race is the only one left, which means the whole country is watching how it ends. Mary's lead has grown in every single post-election count — from 637 votes to more than 4,000, and the preliminary ranked-choice numbers already show her winning. **We are confident Mary Peltola will be the next U.S. Senator from Alaska.** But confidence isn't certification.
