Election night, Columbus, November 3, 2026.
Republicans across Ohio discovered a brand-new party tradition: standing around a television while the governor's mansion changed hands for the first time in twenty years. Dr. Amy Acton -- the physician who once merely asked Ohioans to wash their hands -- beat Donald Trump's hand-picked heir, Vivek Ramaswamy, roughly five points clear when the AP called it (50.8% to 45.9%, with ballots still landing). First Democrat to win the office in two decades. First woman ever elected to it. And the question ricocheting around every county GOP pancake breakfast since is the one you're already asking: did Vivek vote for Amy too?
**Who Is This Guy, You Ask?**
Ramaswamy arrived in Ohio politics the way he arrives everywhere: early, loudly, and carrying a book he wrote about himself. A Cincinnati-raised biotech entrepreneur, he made one fortune founding drug companies and a second fortune explaining, in bestsellers like 'Woke, Inc.', that corporate America had lost its soul. He ran for president in 2024 on a platform of out-talking the entire debate stage, dropped out, endorsed Trump, was briefly handed half of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), then noticed the Ohio governor's office opening up and declared in February 2025. He had never held elected office before this race. He fixed that by also not holding it after.
**The Foisting**
In fairness, Trump didn't just back Ramaswamy -- he and Ohio's own vice president, JD Vance, made repeated pilgrimages to the state to sell him. The pitch amounted to: this candidate comes pre-approved; skip the inspection. Ohio Republicans, obedient in federal elections, were asked to swallow a nominee who had never run for anything they vote on, and whose brand was Wall Street memoirs and debate-stage speed runs. Ohioans have returned bigger products with better marketing.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/349fe5ad-05c9-4a1e-99a8-f201f06356d8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Assessing the Campaign (Republicans, Look Away)**
\- The primary stumble. A YouTube car reviewer, Casey "The Car Guy" Putsch, spent about $130,000 and pulled nearly 18% of the Republican primary vote -- while lobbing veiled ethnic and religious attacks at the Hindu nominee. When a fifth of your base would rather vote for a man who reviews sedans for the algorithm, that is not a campaign; it is a cry for help.
\- The endorsement that wasn't. After losing, Putsch announced he would vote for Amy Acton. So the fellow who ran against Vivek publicly promised his ballot to Amy. Vivek, to his credit, merely lost.
\- **One hundred million dollars**. That is what was spent against Acton. She still won -- the most expensive door Ohio Republicans have ever knocked on, and had slammed shut.
\- The estranged-mother ad. In a race about groceries and rent, the Ramaswamy campaign released a deeply personal attack ad featuring Acton's own estranged mother. Ohio voters -- polite, practical, famously unwilling to be lectured -- treated it like bringing up someone's divorce at Thanksgiving. The ad did not merely miss; it made the target sympathetic.
\- The wrong conversation. The election's central theme was the cost of living. The author of 'Woke, Inc.' kept arriving to a cost-of-living election with a culture-war suitcase. Acton -- a self-described scrappy kid from Youngstown -- talked pharmacies and paychecks; Vivek talked, mostly, about Vivek.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e7cf7192-c4ba-4b74-be70-cd0f802a4de1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**So Has Ohio Turned Blue?**
The boast "more congressional Democrats than ever before" is, historically speaking, nonsense -- Democrats once owned most of Ohio's congressional map. But 2026 was their best night in a generation: they flipped two U.S. House districts, leaving the delegation at 7-7 with Mike Turner's Dayton-area seat still in limbo (by Signal Cleveland's count, Democrats have won eight of fifteen). Brian Poindexter took the 7th District off incumbent Max Miller. Down-ballot, Democrats shattered the Republicans' 65-34 state House supermajority, nicked a couple of state Senate seats, and nearly swept the statewide offices. So no, Ohio is not blue forever. Just blue enough to make Vivek a trivia answer.
**So -- Did He Vote for Her?**
Noone will ever know; the ballot is secret, and Vivek has said only that he is "rooting" for the state and for Acton -- which in Ohio is close enough to an endorsement that several county chairs have filed it as one. What can be certified: his own primary rival pledged his vote to Amy, his own party's base declined to fully show up for him, and the state Trump foisted him upon elected his opponent. If he did quietly vote for Amy, history will remember it as the only decision of his campaign that worked.
**The Post-Mortem Memo Nobody at GOP HQ Ordered**
1\. Endorsements are not candidacies. A Trump blessing got him through the door; it did not get him elected.
2\. Rile the base, lose the middle. Primary-flavored grievance does not pay the mortgage in Dayton.
3\. Attack ads have recoil. The mother ad converted more Ohioans to Acton than any Acton ad did.
4\. Ohio is not a red state; it is a bored one. Ask it about insurance premiums, not universities.
5\. Money is not message. $100 million bought the best-funded concession speech of the cycle.
Somewhere tonight, Vivek is almost certainly drafting the book about all this. Ohio will read it only if it shows up in the grocery aisle -- which was, notably, his whole problem.

But we want you to know something: **you are not alone.**

You served this country in uniform. You’ve never backed down from a fight. And we won’t back down now either.

**Friday, November 13, 2026**
The morning after the holidays, finding something in the refrigerator is an excavation. You move the mashed potatoes aside, lift a parchment-wrapped bundle you would rather not identify, and work your way toward the back, then down to the bottom, where the good stuff is hiding.
"Get me the stuffing."
"Where is it?"
"In the stainless steel container."
"I do not see it."
"Dig deeper."
We often judge a nation's strength by what is most visible: its economy, institutions, military, and influence. But there is more beneath the surface.
A country is also sustained by families teaching responsibility, people keeping households and communities going, care for the land and resources entrusted to us, and citizens who expect their representatives to answer to them.
These foundations depend on one another.
Government can protect the conditions for a strong society, but it cannot manufacture the relationships, judgment, and responsibility that sustain one.
Where, then, does a nation's strength begin?
**Pause.
Breathe.
Look Deeper.**
**Refuel.**
**Welcome to Sweet Ground.**

Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.) speaks at an event in St. Paul, Minnesota, on August 8, 2026. Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images.
**Friday, November 13, 2026 - **
_**Iran:** Iran destroys U.S. early warning radar in Bahrain, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) says. Another tanker hits mine in Hormuz, IRGC says. Iran tells UN nuclear agency inspections cannot proceed while under threat from U.S. IEA: Global oil market returning to surplus._
_**Palestine:** Israeli military shoots and kills Palestinian in Gaza City. 49 countries call on Israel to allow humanitarian aid into Gaza. Israeli forces conduct raids, arrest Palestinians across occupied West Bank._
_**Yemen:** Saudi-led coalition kills five civilians in Saada. Airlines extend suspension of flights to Saudi Arabia amid continued Ansarallah attacks_
_**Lebanon:** Israel attacks southern Lebanon, again violating so-called ceasefire._
_**U.S.:** Sen. Chris Van Hollen announces he will run for Senate majority leader. CBS: ICE deported a record 483,200 people in 2026. Democrat Mary Peltola maintains lead over Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan in Alaska's Senate race. Politico: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani plans to disband police protest unit. President Donald Trump urges Senate Republicans to pass $350 billion in defense spending. Donald Trump Jr. leaves advisory role at prediction market Kalshi. Families of U.S. Navy sailors told to prepare for 12-month deployment. Trump says possibility of U.S. military operation against Cuba "before I leave."_
_**International:** Drop Site Exclusive: Al-Shabaab ambushes U.S.-trained Somali special forces. Imran Khan's sisters released from prison. Pakistani police and Taliban exchange fire; 10 officers, up to 18 Taliban fighters dead. U.S. State Department releases report on whereabouts of $12 billion taken from Venezuela. Russian court sentences rights lawyer for treason. Russian soldier killed in St. Petersburg car-bombing. Italian schools mostly stay open despite second day of hoax bomb threats. Indonesian vice president resigns; wiretapping investigation ongoing. Former senior Bolivian judge arrested on suspicion of drug trafficking. Sudanese military leader meets with heads of state from Turkey, Pakistan, and Libya at climate summit. UN peacekeepers, South Sudanese authorities failed to prevent massacre in South Sudanese village, Amnesty says._
**This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday**
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZHJvcHNpdGVuZXdzLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.PfXzs5Iq-4tUR7BmNNur8Vs0Nnmi-6BwEPRkxJ7tCIU?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=224766563)
* * *
# Iran
* **Iran destroys U.S. early warning radar in Bahrain, IRGC says:** Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) [said](https://substack.com/redirect/f3b0f230-6ba1-44a4-bfa5-9d4b9a40004a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that it destroyed a U.S. early warning radar system in Bahrain in response to an attack on a telecommunications tower in the southern Iranian port of Sirik on Thursday. Bahrain is home to the U.S. Navy's 5th Fleet. It is the first Iranian attack on Bahrain since September.
* "This serves as a serious warning to the aggressor enemy to cease its aerial provocations and oil smuggling in the Strait of Hormuz. Should these violations and acts of aggression recur, the IRGC Aerospace Force stands in full readiness to engage without limits," the IRGC said.
* Iran's navy also said that it shot down an U.S. MQ-1 Predator drone over the Strait of Hormuz, the state-aligned Islamic Republic News Agency reported. The drone was downed on the southern Sirik coast.
* **Another tanker hits mine in Hormuz, IRGC says:** A liquefied petroleum gas tanker struck a mine in the Strait of Hormuz, causing an explosion, the IRGC said, adding that the Iranian navy sent repeated warnings against using an "unauthorized" south passage through the strait.
* **Iran tells UN nuclear agency inspections cannot proceed while under threat from U.S.:** Iran told the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) this month that discussions on nuclear monitoring cannot proceed while it is under threat from military attacks, the Associated Press [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/4b83acdc-a4f2-40ad-a4cb-ec3acf95e3f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), citing a confidential report by the IAEA circulated to member states on Friday.
* Iran said that discussions on nuclear inspections cannot resume amid "a series of persistent, explicit, and public threats by the President of the United States of America . . . to commit further acts of armed aggression" against Iran, "particularly targeting its nuclear facilities."
* In a letter to the IAEA, Iran expressed concern about the U.S. State Department's recent announcement that it would pay up to $20 million for information on Iran's nuclear program.
* Iran has not granted IAEA inspectors access to nuclear sites targeted by Israel and the U.S. during the 12-day war in June 2025. The IAEA expressed "increasing concern" about a fuel enrichment plant in Isfahan. Inspectors were due to visit the facility on the day the U.S.-Israeli strikes began in June, but cancelled the inspection. The IAEA said in its report that it "does not know" the site's "exact location or whether it contains nuclear material."
* **IEA: Global oil market returning to surplus:** The global oil market will return to a surplus in the fourth quarter of 2026, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said in its monthly oil. Exports from the Middle East are recovering despite continued attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.
* "The oil market is showing tentative signs of rebalancing, with global oil supplies surpassing demand for the first time since the outbreak of the war in Iran," the IEA said.

# Palestine
* **Israeli military shoots and kills Palestinian in Gaza City:** A Palestinian was killed by Israeli gunfire in the Tuffah neighborhood of Gaza City on Friday morning, according to Al Jazeera.
* **49 countries call on Israel to allow humanitarian aid into Gaza:** On Thursday, 49 countries issued a joint [statement](https://substack.com/redirect/b9f95f74-68d5-47b0-a02a-9e766db399d6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) urging Israel to ease its restrictions on aid, warning that its near-total blockade was worsening public-health conditions in Gaza.
* The signatories called on Israel to allow aid to enter Gaza unhindered, demanding that it reopen humanitarian corridors and approve essential supplies, including so-called "dual-use items" that Israel bans from entering Gaza.
* "As winter sets in, far too many people in Gaza are still without adequate shelter, and risk exposure to hypothermia, respiratory infections, waterborne diseases and other preventable illnesses," Britain's ambassador to the United Nations, Sarah MacIntosh, said at the UN headquarters in New York on Thursday.
* The appeal specifically emphasized supplies needed for shelter, fuel, water, sanitation, and medical care. It also called on Israel to allow medical patients in Gaza to receive care in East Jerusalem and the West Bank.
* The countries also noted that medical and humanitarian workers and facilities must be protected, urged expedited criminal investigations into Israeli attacks on medical personnel, and demanded that Israel grant senior international delegations and journalists access to Gaza.
* The initiative was led by Britain, Qatar, and Jordan and backed by countries including Australia, Canada, Egypt, France, Italy, the Netherlands, Poland, Saudi Arabia, Spain, and Turkey. The United States did not sign the statement.
* **Israeli forces conduct raids, arrest Palestinians across occupied West Bank:** Israeli forces conducted raids and arrested Palestinians across the occupied West Bank on Friday, WAFA [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/c29ebb63-53bd-4b53-8ba2-97003ae26652?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
* Israeli soldiers arrested four Palestinians in towns around the city of Jenin.
* Troops stormed the town of Al-Ubeidiya, east of Bethlehem, firing sound bombs and taking up positions in the town. They raided several neighborhoods in Nablus, and searched homes in the nearby towns of Beit Furik and Beit Dajan.
* The Israeli army invaded the village of Marda, north of Salfit, with soldiers searching a large number of homes, detaining a number of young men, and subjecting them to field interrogations before releasing them.

# Yemen
* **Saudi-led coalition kills five civilians in Saada:** Shelling by the Saudi-led coalition in the northern governorate of Saada killed five civilians on Friday, Al Jazeera reported.
* Ansarallah carried out raids on sites in Taiz and attacked government military camps with six ballistic missiles, Al Jazeera reported, citing Ansarallah sources.
* **Airlines extend suspension of flights to Saudi Arabia amid continued Ansarallah attacks:** International airlines extended flight suspensions to several cities in Saudi Arabia as Ansarallah targets airports, energy facilities, and infrastructure in missile and drone attacks.
* Several Indian airlines announced that flights to Saudi cities including Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam, and Medina would remain suspended until late November. Emirati and Omani carriers announced similar extensions.
* KLM has cancelled service to late November while British Airways postponed the resumption of its London-Riyadh route until January 2027.

# Lebanon
* **Israel attacks southern Lebanon, again violating so-called ceasefire:** The Israeli military shelled several towns in southern Lebanon on Friday, the Lebanese government-aligned National News Agency reported. Among the towns Israel attacked were Mayfadoun, Talloussah, and Bani Haiyyan. No casualties were reported.

# U.S. News
* **Sen. Chris Van Hollen announces he will run for Senate majority leader:** Maryland Democratic Sen. **Chris Van Hollen** [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/e379565a-f086-4137-80ff-82302b63f542?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that he will challenge Sen. **Chuck Schumer** (D-N.Y.) for Senate majority leader. In an announcement on Thursday, Van Hollen said that "the American people called for change" in the midterms, adding that the Democratic Party "needs new leadership." He said that if he was elected, he would use every tool available to the majority to end the Iran War, including leveraging a December funding deadline. Sen. **Bernie Sanders** (I-Vt.) and Sen.-elect **Abdul El-Sayed** (D-Mich.) endorsed him after his announcement, while Sens. **Angus King** (I-Maine) and **Kirsten Gillibrand** (D-N.Y.) criticized Van Hollen's challenge and defended Schumer as an architect of sweeping Democratic wins in the midterms. Congressional Democrats will choose their leaders in a closed-door caucus in December. To become the party's majority leader, Schumer or Van Hollen will need the support of 28 of the party's 55 Senators.
* Keep track of where senators stand on the leadership vote with **[Drop Site's Whip Count](https://substack.com/redirect/29436897-1224-4e03-8c25-1d4161ca778b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**.
* **CBS: ICE deported a record 483,200 people in 2026:** Immigration and Customs Enforcement [deported](https://substack.com/redirect/19b63e10-f689-48bf-8776-4cda30ef82a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a record 483,200 people in fiscal year 2026, according to Homeland Security data obtained by CBS. The total tops the prior record of 442,640 ICE deportees in the 2025 fiscal year. The nonpartisan Migration Policy Institute found that only about 20% of roughly 980,000 ICE and CBP deportees since January 2025 had ever been convicted of a crime. Exit polls from the midterm elections showed that voters rejected the Trump administration's far-right immigration policies.
* **Peltola maintains lead over Sullivan in Alaska 's Senate race: **As of Friday morning,**** Democratic Senate nominee **Mary Peltola** [leads](https://substack.com/redirect/83db51b5-59e0-4c6d-9152-b575241390af?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Republican Sen. **Dan Sullivan** by 3,975 votes in Alaska's Senate race, which has not been called. According to data from Decision Desk HQ, Peltola has received over 48.5% of votes, and Sullivan has received over 46.9%. Tens of thousands of ballots from Anchorage and other rural areas have yet to be counted.
* **Politico: Mamdani plans to disband the NYPD 's protest unit:** New York City Mayor **Zohran Mamdani** plans to [disband](https://substack.com/redirect/f98f82a0-699d-47ef-961c-2a1f793cea41?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the New York Police Department's Strategic Response Group, a controversial crowd-control unit that has repeatedly cracked down on nonviolent protesters, Politico reported. A formal announcement is expected as early as next week. Civil-rights advocates and activists have accused the police unit of excessive force and misconduct. NYPD Commissioner **Jessica Tisch** has supported keeping the SRG unit.
* **Trump urges Senate Republicans to pass $350 billion in defense spending:** On Thursday, President Donald Trump [said](https://substack.com/redirect/4ca53a24-e54c-49f2-b456-0ebcbba4b94e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Republican legislators must pass a new $350 billion in defense spending before losing their Congressional majority. "Republicans must deliver for our Warriors. The Democrats never will. The time is NOW," Trump [wrote](https://substack.com/redirect/53a81d62-b111-4441-9258-c43fdc6e5c23?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Truth Social on Thursday. A budget outlined passed by the House includes Iran war funding, but it has stalled in the Senate for almost four months. The budget outline provides $60 billion for the Pentagon.
* **Donald Trump Jr. leaves advisory role at prediction market Kalshi: Donald Trump Jr.** is [leaving](https://substack.com/redirect/7b8f78c3-63e2-4d94-b5ee-952fc3af7452?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) his advisory role at the prediction market Kalshi, Bloomberg reported. A Kalshi spokesperson said that Trump Jr. and Kalshia "mutually agreed to end Don's advisory role after his firm's significant investment in a competitor this past summer," a reference to his firm 1789 Capital's stake in the rival prediction company Polymarket, where he is also an adviser.
* **Families of U.S. Navy sailors told to prepare for 12-month deployment:** At a November 9 town hall, Navy leaders [said](https://substack.com/redirect/c8e76071-b15b-42ca-9cb7-76718d6ada83?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that the USS George H.W. Bush aircraft carrier will not be home for the holidays. Acting Secretary of the Navy **Hung Cao** told families at the town hall that the soldiers would return home when there is a "non-nuclear Iran." The carrier left Naval Station Norfolk, in Virginia, for the Middle East on March 31. At the time, its deployment was expected to last six or seven months. The Navy said that War Secretary **Pete Hegseth** would decide when to bring the carrier home from the Middle East.
* **Trump says possibility of U.S. military operation against Cuba "before I leave": **Asked on Thursday about a military operation against Cuba, President Trump [said](https://substack.com/redirect/6365a238-6d68-4b85-ac9a-878b6c572582?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), "I would like to be able to do it," adding that he wants to "get Cuba done before I leave." Trump said that Secretary of State **Marco Rubio** was the administration's leader on the issue. Earlier this week, Trump told reporters at the White House that the Cuban government would fall "very soon," and last week at Mar-a-Lago he said that Rubio was "going to work on Cuba."

📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com.
# Other International News
* **Exclusive: Al-Shabaab ambushes U.S.-trained Somali special forces:** Al-Shabaab fighters ambushed U.S.-trained Somali forces near the town of Yaqbirweyne, in the volatile Lower Shabelle region, on Thursday, Drop Site News contributor Mohamed Gabobe reports.**** A five-vehicle convoy of Danab ("Lightning") Brigade forces was ambushed during a routine patrol, two Somali security officials told Drop Site. The Danab is an elite indigenous counter-terrorism force that the U.S. helped create during the second administration of Barack Obama. It is explicitly tasked with fighting Al-Shabaab. Eight soldiers were killed in the fighting, the officials said, and Al-Shabaab seized two of the convoy's vehicles. The militant group claimed to have killed 17 Danab troops. According to the Somali Ministry of Defense, two high-ranking field commanders were among the dead.
* The ambush occurred near a recently abandoned U.S. military base, the Baledogle Airfield, that is about 60 miles from Mogadishu, the capital of Somalia. Earlier this month, the U.S. confirmed its withdrawal from the base. "The relocation from Baledogle was 100% an economic decision," Army Lt. Gen. John Brennan, deputy commander of the U.S. military's Africa command, [told reporters](https://substack.com/redirect/d29e6c33-5d1e-4337-92cc-468b8091ea37?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) this month. "The surface of the airfield was declining to the point where it was becoming dangerous to land aircraft there." Baledogle was the largest U.S. military base in Somalia.
* In September, Mohamed Gabobe reported in Drop Site News that the U.S. military is constructing a new base in Bosaso, Somalia, a port city on the shores of the Gulf of Aden. **Read the full story[here](https://substack.com/redirect/cc352f0e-5e00-4602-a370-be4a8513092d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**
* **Imran Khan 's sisters released from prison: **Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi Khan, two sisters of former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan, were [released](https://substack.com/redirect/85675cb7-833f-49b1-9fed-abf433fd49ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from prison after 53 days, their lawyer said on Thursday. Their third sister, Aleema Khan, remains in prison. The three sisters were arrested a week before a planned September 27 march demanding the release of their brother Imran Khan, who has been imprisoned since August 2023. The march, organized by his Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf Party (PTI), was canceled after the federal government suspended the PTI-led government in the province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Last month, Drop Site contributor Mehr Sher reported on the Pakistani government's violent crackdown in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. **Read the full story[here](https://substack.com/redirect/cb906146-2239-4cd8-8efb-077363ae29e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**
* **Pakistani police and Taliban exchange fire; 10 officers, up to 18 Taliban fighters dead:** Pakistani Taliban fighters [attacked](https://substack.com/redirect/a6d1d036-8df8-4d40-a6a7-f828dbb0209f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) police officers in the Kohat area of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, on Thursday. Ten police officers and 18 Taliban gunmen were killed, according to provincial police, and 12 police officers were wounded. The attack occurred as police**** officers were returning from a mine in the Gumbat area on Wednesday.
* **U.S. State Department releases report on whereabouts of $12 billion taken from Venezuela:** On Thursday, the State Department [released](https://substack.com/redirect/fb280726-0cbd-44c6-a5aa-c5a4a1f45ff0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a 53-page report outlining the U.S. government's disbursement of over $12 billion in oil and mineral revenue that it has seized from Venezuela since U.S. forces abducted President Nicolas Maduro in January. Of the total sum seized, $169 million remains unaccounted for. The State Department report is heavily redacted, and the identities of many relevant parties to the transactions are unknown. According to the report, as of September almost all of the seized funds were sent to Venezuelan banks, which used foreign-currency exchanges to prop up the Venezuelan bolivar, the country's currency.
* **Russian court sentences rights lawyer for treason:** On Thursday, a court in the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad [sentenced](https://substack.com/redirect/37cf106c-3313-4828-9f58-ae39e053bade?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Maria Bontsler, a 66-year-old rights lawyer, to 12 years in prison, plus a year of "restrictions" on her freedom, for treason. Prosecutors accused her of relaying information about criminal cases in Kaliningrad to Ukraine. The rights group Slovo Zashchite said that Bontsler had defended several defendants in political cases, and that her trial was held behind closed doors. Bontsler and her lawyers were barred from attending the trial, the group added, and their participation was limited to presenting a closing statement. Russian courts have previously imprisoned lawyers who take politically sensitive cases, as in the 2025 cases of three lawyers who represented the opposition leader Alexey Navalny, who was killed by poisoning in 2024.
* **Russian soldier killed in St. Petersburg car-bombing:** A Russian soldier was [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/6763758e-f3b6-4b4f-b2e4-32cdf359f732?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) after the SUV he was driving exploded in St. Petersburg, Russia, Reuters reported. Russian police are investigating the killing as a murder. The Russian newspaper Fontanka reported that a 31-year-old suspect planted the bomb under the car of the soldier, said to be a colonel, after conducting at least a month of surveillance. The suspect has fled the country, according to the paper. In August, a Russian serviceman died in a car explosion in St. Petersburg.
* **Italian schools mostly stay open despite second day of hoax bomb threats** : More than 3,700 Italian schools [received](https://substack.com/redirect/5005bcff-9c86-455c-a034-351d8c01bb6c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) bomb threats on Thursday, but only 77 schools were evacuated, after Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said that only the threats with "concrete elements beyond the mere receipt of a mass email" should be taken seriously. About 6,300 schools received bomb threats on Wednesday. The emails were signed by "Mikhail Andropov," and threatened Meloni herself. Schools in Scotland, Northern Ireland, and Ireland received similar emails but remained in session.
* **Indonesian vice president resigns; wiretapping investigation ongoing:** Indonesia's Vice President, Gibran Rakabuming Raka, stepped down on Thursday. He said that he resigned to avoid a prolonged political controversy, though a cabinet minister present at a meeting where his resignation was discussed said that President Prabowo Subianto urged Gibran to defend himself.
* Separately on Thursday, Indonesian police announced that they gathered enough initial evidence to pursue treason charges against four suspects accused of wiretapping Prabowo. Former police chief Listyo Sigit Prabowo (of no relation to the president) and three senior police officials were arrested last week over suspicion that they monitored phones belonging to President Prabowo, other government officials, activists, and journalists. Listyo Prabowo was a close advisor to President Prabowo.
* **Former senior Bolivian judge arrested on suspicion of drug trafficking:** On Wednesday, Bolivian authorities [arrested](https://substack.com/redirect/c8c96939-b628-4ac7-8f54-c1cfbe5bcb58?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Aldo Quezada, the former chief justice of the Santa Cruz departmental court, on suspicion of drug trafficking. He resigned last month after the U.S. restricted his visa over alleged links to drug traffickers. The U.S. government's visa-restrictions list has also targeted officials in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru. Quezada is one of several senior Bolivian judicial officials arrested since September. Former Attorney General Roger Mariaca was arrested on September 30 on suspicion of money laundering and drug trafficking. Right-wing President Rodrigo Paz, who took office in November 2025, has sought closer ties with the U.S. Last month, Drop Site's Jose Luis Granada Ceja reported on the arrest of Mariaca and the selective use of drug-trafficking accusations to advance U.S. interests in Latin America. **Read the full story[here](https://substack.com/redirect/b50007d0-6c41-40f7-9676-b73650e8f7f1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**
* **Sudanese military leader meets with heads of state from Turkey, Pakistan, and Libya at climate summit:** Sudanese army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan [met](https://substack.com/redirect/06a58049-a34b-4adb-831f-e66f5caeedda?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with Turkish President Recep Erdogan, Pakistani President Shehbaz Sharif, and Libyan Prime Minister Abdulhamid Dbeibah on the sidelines of the COP31 climate summit in Turkey on Thursday. Al-Burhan's office said that the meetings focused on political and security issues in Sudan and diplomatic and economic relations among the countries.
* **UN peacekeepers, South Sudanese authorities failed to prevent massacre in South Sudanese village, Amnesty says:** The UN Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS) was [warned](https://substack.com/redirect/0552cf9f-c599-4887-9a8b-cc0166d87f1a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) about a March 2026 attack in Abiemnom, South Sudan, but did not reinforce its peacekeeping ranks until after the attack, Amnesty International said in a report on Thursday. As many as 1,500 armed men attacked the village of Abiemnom, shooting residents, burning more than 230 structures, and looting a hospital. More than 200 people died. After Amnesty released the report, a UNMISS spokesperson said that cuts to the UN peacekeeping force's budget required the force to concentrate on protecting about 2,500 people sheltering at its base. The spokesperson said that UNMISS repeatedly asked the South Sudanese army for more forces. The UN Security Council renewed the UNMISS mandate in April, but cut its troop count from 17,000 to 12,000.

Friday, November 13, 2026 - Iran: Iran destroys U.S. early warning radar in Bahrain, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) says. Another tanker hits mine in Hormuz, IRGC says. Iran tells UN nuclear agency inspections cannot proceed while under threat from U.S. IEA: Global oil market returning to surplus. Palestine: Israeli military shoots and kills Palestinian in Gaza City. 49 countries call on Israel to allow humanitarian aid into Gaza. Israeli forces conduct raids, arrest Palestinians across occupied West Bank. Yemen: Saudi-led coalition kills five civilians in Saada. Airlines extend suspension of flights to Saudi Arabia amid continued Ansarallah attacks Lebanon: Israel attacks southern Lebanon, again violating so-called ceasefire. U.S.: Sen. Chris Van Hollen announces he will run for Senate majority leader. CBS: ICE deported a record 483,200 people in 2026. Democrat Mary Peltola maintains lead over Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan in Alaska's Senate race. Politico: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani plans to disband police protest unit. President Donald Trump urges Senate Republicans to pass $350 billion in defense spending. Donald Trump Jr. leaves advisory role at prediction market Kalshi. Families of U.S. Navy sailors told to prepare for 12-month deployment. Trump says possibility of U.S. military operation against Cuba "before I leave." Russian court sentences rights lawyer for treason. Russian soldier killed in St. Petersburg car-bombing. Italian schools mostly stay open despite second day of hoax bomb threats. Indonesian vice president resigns; wiretapping investigation ongoing. Former senior Bolivian judge arrested on suspicion of drug trafficking. This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Iran Iran destroys U.S. early warning radar in Bahrain, IRGC says: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) that it destroyed a U.S. early warning radar system in Bahrain in response to an attack on a telecommunications tower in the southern Iranian port of Sirik on Thursday. Bahrain is home to the U.S. Navy's 5th Fleet. It is the first Iranian attack on Bahrain since September. "This serves as a serious warning to the aggressor enemy to cease its aerial provocations and oil smuggling in the Strait of Hormuz. Should these violations and acts of aggression recur, the IRGC Aerospace Force stands in full readiness to engage without limits," the IRGC said. Iran's navy also said that it shot down an U.S. MQ-1 Predator drone over the Strait of Hormuz, the state-aligned Islamic Republic News Agency reported. The drone was downed on the southern Sirik coast. Another tanker hits mine in Hormuz, IRGC says: A liquefied petroleum gas tanker struck a mine in the Strait of Hormuz, causing an explosion, the IRGC said, adding that the Iranian navy sent repeated warnings against using an "unauthorized" south passage through the strait. Iran tells UN nuclear agency inspections cannot proceed while under threat from U.S.: Iran told the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) this month that discussions on nuclear monitoring cannot proceed while it is under threat from military attacks, the Associated Press , citing a confidential report by the IAEA circulated to member states on Friday. Iran said that discussions on nuclear inspections cannot resume amid "a series of persistent, explicit, and public threats by the President of the United States of America . . . to commit further acts of armed aggression" against Iran, "particularly targeting its nuclear facilities." In a letter to the IAEA, Iran expressed concern about the U.S. State Department's recent announcement that it would pay up to $20 million for information on Iran's nuclear program. Iran has not granted IAEA inspectors access to nuclear sites targeted by Israel and the U.S. during the 12-day war in June 2025. The IAEA expressed "increasing concern" about a fuel enrichment plant in Isfahan. Inspectors were due to visit the facility on the day the U.S.-Israeli strikes began in June, but cancelled the inspection. The IAEA said in its report that it "does not know" the site's "exact location or whether it contains nuclear material." IEA: Global oil market returning to surplus: The global oil market will return to a surplus in the fourth quarter of 2026, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said in its monthly oil. Exports from the Middle East are recovering despite continued attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. "The oil market is showing tentative signs of rebalancing, with global oil supplies surpassing demand for the first time since the outbreak of the war in Iran," the IEA said. Palestine Israeli military shoots and kills Palestinian in Gaza City: A Palestinian was killed by Israeli gunfire in the Tuffah neighborhood of Gaza City on Friday morning, according to Al Jazeera. 49 countries call on Israel to allow humanitarian aid into Gaza: On Thursday, 49 countries issued a joint urging Israel to ease its restrictions on aid, warning that its near-total blockade was worsening public-health conditions in Gaza. The signatories called on Israel to allow aid to enter Gaza unhindered, demanding that it reopen humanitarian corridors and approve essential supplies, including so-called "dual-use items" that Israel bans from entering Gaza. "As winter sets in, far too many people in Gaza are still without adequate shelter, and risk exposure to hypothermia, respiratory infections, waterborne diseases and other preventable illnesses," Britain's ambassador to the United Nations, Sarah MacIntosh, said at the UN headquarters in New York on Thursday. The appeal specifically emphasized supplies needed for shelter, fuel, water, sanitation, and medical care. It also called on Israel to allow medical patients in Gaza to receive care in East Jerusalem and the West Bank. The countries also noted that medical and humanitarian workers and facilities must be protected, urged expedited criminal investigations into Israeli attacks on medical personnel, and demanded that Israel grant senior international delegations and journalists access to Gaza. The initiative was led by Britain, Qatar, and Jordan and backed by countries including Australia, Canada, Egypt, France, Italy, the Netherlands, Poland, Saudi Arabia, Spain, and Turkey. The United States did not sign the statement. Israeli forces conduct raids, arrest Palestinians across occupied West Bank: Israeli forces conducted raids and arrested Palestinians across the occupied West Bank on Friday, WAFA . Israeli soldiers arrested four Palestinians in towns around the city of Jenin. Troops stormed the town of Al-Ubeidiya, east of Bethlehem, firing sound bombs and taking up positions in the town. They raided several neighborhoods in Nablus, and searched homes in the nearby towns of Beit Furik and Beit Dajan. The Israeli army invaded the village of Marda, north of Salfit, with soldiers searching a large number of homes, detaining a number of young men, and subjecting them to field interrogations before releasing them. Yemen Saudi-led coalition kills five civilians in Saada: Shelling by the Saudi-led coalition in the northern governorate of Saada killed five civilians on Friday, Al Jazeera reported. Ansarallah carried out raids on sites in Taiz and attacked government military camps with six ballistic missiles, Al Jazeera reported, citing Ansarallah sources. Airlines extend suspension of flights to Saudi Arabia amid continued Ansarallah attacks: International airlines extended flight suspensions to several cities in Saudi Arabia as Ansarallah targets airports, energy facilities, and infrastructure in missile and drone attacks. Several Indian airlines announced that flights to Saudi cities including Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam, and Medina would remain suspended until late November. Emirati and Omani carriers announced similar extensions. KLM has cancelled service to late November while British Airways postponed the resumption of its London-Riyadh route until January 2027. Lebanon Israel attacks southern Lebanon, again violating so-called ceasefire: The Israeli military shelled several towns in southern Lebanon on Friday, the Lebanese government-aligned National News Agency reported. Among the towns Israel attacked were Mayfadoun, Talloussah, and Bani Haiyyan. No casualties were reported. U.S. News Sen. Chris Van Hollen announces he will run for Senate majority leader: Maryland Democratic Sen. Chris Van Hollen that he will challenge Sen. Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) for Senate majority leader. In an announcement on Thursday, Van Hollen said that "the American people called for change" in the midterms, adding that the Democratic Party "needs new leadership." He said that if he was elected, he would use every tool available to the majority to end the Iran War, including leveraging a December funding deadline. Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) and Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed (D-Mich.) endorsed him after his announcement, while Sens. Angus King (I-Maine) and Kirsten Gillibrand (D-N.Y.) criticized Van Hollen's challenge and defended Schumer as an architect of sweeping Democratic wins in the midterms. Congressional Democrats will choose their leaders in a closed-door caucus in December. To become the party's majority leader, Schumer or Van Hollen will need the support of 28 of the party's 55 Senators. Keep track of where senators stand on the leadership vote with . CBS: ICE deported a record 483,200 people in 2026: Immigration and Customs Enforcement a record 483,200 people in fiscal year 2026, according to Homeland Security data obtained by CBS. The total tops the prior record of 442,640 ICE deportees in the 2025 fiscal year. The nonpartisan Migration Policy Institute found that only about 20% of roughly 980,000 ICE and CBP deportees since January 2025 had ever been convicted of a crime. Exit polls from the midterm elections showed that voters rejected the Trump administration's far-right immigration policies. Peltola maintains lead over Sullivan in Alaska 's Senate race: As of Friday morning,** Democratic Senate nominee Mary Peltola Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan by 3,975 votes in Alaska's Senate race, which has not been called. According to data from Decision Desk HQ, Peltola has received over 48.5% of votes, and Sullivan has received over 46.9%. Tens of thousands of ballots from Anchorage and other rural areas have yet to be counted. Politico: Mamdani plans to disband the NYPD 's protest unit: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani plans to the New York Police Department's Strategic Response Group, a controversial crowd-control unit that has repeatedly cracked down on nonviolent protesters, Politico reported. A formal announcement is expected as early as next week. Civil-rights advocates and activists have accused the police unit of excessive force and misconduct. NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch has supported keeping the SRG unit. Trump urges Senate Republicans to pass $350 billion in defense spending: On Thursday, President Donald Trump that Republican legislators must pass a new $350 billion in defense spending before losing their Congressional majority. "Republicans must deliver for our Warriors. The Democrats never will. The time is NOW," Trump on Truth Social on Thursday. A budget outlined passed by the House includes Iran war funding, but it has stalled in the Senate for almost four months. The budget outline provides $60 billion for the Pentagon. Donald Trump Jr. leaves advisory role at prediction market Kalshi: Donald Trump Jr. is his advisory role at the prediction market Kalshi, Bloomberg reported. A Kalshi spokesperson said that Trump Jr. and Kalshia "mutually agreed to end Don's advisory role after his firm's significant investment in a competitor this past summer," a reference to his firm 1789 Capital's stake in the rival prediction company Polymarket, where he is also an adviser. Families of U.S. Navy sailors told to prepare for 12-month deployment: At a November 9 town hall, Navy leaders that the USS George H.W. Bush aircraft carrier will not be home for the holidays. Acting Secretary of the Navy Hung Cao told families at the town hall that the soldiers would return home when there is a "non-nuclear Iran." The carrier left Naval Station Norfolk, in Virginia, for the Middle East on March 31. At the time, its deployment was expected to last six or seven months. The Navy said that War Secretary Pete Hegseth would decide when to bring the carrier home from the Middle East. Trump says possibility of U.S. military operation against Cuba "before I leave": Asked on Thursday about a military operation against Cuba, President Trump , "I would like to be able to do it," adding that he wants to "get Cuba done before I leave." Trump said that Secretary of State Marco Rubio was the administration's leader on the issue. Earlier this week, Trump told reporters at the White House that the Cuban government would fall "very soon," and last week at Mar-a-Lago he said that Rubio was "going to work on Cuba." 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com. Other International News Exclusive: Al-Shabaab ambushes U.S.-trained Somali special forces: Al-Shabaab fighters ambushed U.S.-trained Somali forces near the town of Yaqbirweyne, in the volatile Lower Shabelle region, on Thursday, Drop Site News contributor Mohamed Gabobe reports. A five-vehicle convoy of Danab ("Lightning") Brigade forces was ambushed during a routine patrol, two Somali security officials told Drop Site. The Danab is an elite indigenous counter-terrorism force that the U.S. helped create during the second administration of Barack Obama. It is explicitly tasked with fighting Al-Shabaab. Eight soldiers were killed in the fighting, the officials said, and Al-Shabaab seized two of the convoy's vehicles. The militant group claimed to have killed 17 Danab troops. According to the Somali Ministry of Defense, two high-ranking field commanders were among the dead. The ambush occurred near a recently abandoned U.S. military base, the Baledogle Airfield, that is about 60 miles from Mogadishu, the capital of Somalia. Earlier this month, the U.S. confirmed its withdrawal from the base. "The relocation from Baledogle was 100% an economic decision," Army Lt. Gen. John Brennan, deputy commander of the U.S. military's Africa command, this month. "The surface of the airfield was declining to the point where it was becoming dangerous to land aircraft there." Baledogle was the largest U.S. military base in Somalia. In September, Mohamed Gabobe reported in Drop Site News that the U.S. military is constructing a new base in Bosaso, Somalia, a port city on the shores of the Gulf of Aden. Read the full story. Imran Khan 's sisters released from prison: Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi Khan, two sisters of former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan, were from prison after 53 days, their lawyer said on Thursday. Their third sister, Aleema Khan, remains in prison. The three sisters were arrested a week before a planned September 27 march demanding the release of their brother Imran Khan, who has been imprisoned since August 2023. The march, organized by his Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf Party (PTI), was canceled after the federal government suspended the PTI-led government in the province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Last month, Drop Site contributor Mehr Sher reported on the Pakistani government's violent crackdown in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Read the full story. Pakistani police and Taliban exchange fire; 10 officers, up to 18 Taliban fighters dead: Pakistani Taliban fighters police officers in the Kohat area of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, on Thursday. Ten police officers and 18 Taliban gunmen were killed, according to provincial police, and 12 police officers were wounded. The attack occurred as police officers were returning from a mine in the Gumbat area on Wednesday. U.S. State Department releases report on whereabouts of $12 billion taken from Venezuela: On Thursday, the State Department a 53-page report outlining the U.S. government's disbursement of over $12 billion in oil and mineral revenue that it has seized from Venezuela since U.S. forces abducted President Nicolas Maduro in January. Of the total sum seized, $169 million remains unaccounted for. The State Department report is heavily redacted, and the identities of many relevant parties to the transactions are unknown. According to the report, as of September almost all of the seized funds were sent to Venezuelan banks, which used foreign-currency exchanges to prop up the Venezuelan bolivar, the country's currency. Russian court sentences rights lawyer for treason: On Thursday, a court in the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad Maria Bontsler, a 66-year-old rights lawyer, to 12 years in prison, plus a year of "restrictions" on her freedom, for treason. Prosecutors accused her of relaying information about criminal cases in Kaliningrad to Ukraine. The rights group Slovo Zashchite said that Bontsler had defended several defendants in political cases, and that her trial was held behind closed doors. Bontsler and her lawyers were barred from attending the trial, the group added, and their participation was limited to presenting a closing statement. Russian courts have previously imprisoned lawyers who take politically sensitive cases, as in the 2025 cases of three lawyers who represented the opposition leader Alexey Navalny, who was killed by poisoning in 2024. Russian soldier killed in St. Petersburg car-bombing: A Russian soldier was after the SUV he was driving exploded in St. Petersburg, Russia, Reuters reported. Russian police are investigating the killing as a murder. The Russian newspaper Fontanka reported that a 31-year-old suspect planted the bomb under the car of the soldier, said to be a colonel, after conducting at least a month of surveillance. The suspect has fled the country, according to the paper. In August, a Russian serviceman died in a car explosion in St. Petersburg. Italian schools mostly stay open despite second day of hoax bomb threats : More than 3,700 Italian schools bomb threats on Thursday, but only 77 schools were evacuated, after Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said that only the threats with "concrete elements beyond the mere receipt of a mass email" should be taken seriously. About 6,300 schools received bomb threats on Wednesday. The emails were signed by "Mikhail Andropov," and threatened Meloni herself. Schools in Scotland, Northern Ireland, and Ireland received similar emails but remained in session. Indonesian vice president resigns; wiretapping investigation ongoing: Indonesia's Vice President, Gibran Rakabuming Raka, stepped down on Thursday. He said that he resigned to avoid a prolonged political controversy, though a cabinet minister present at a meeting where his resignation was discussed said that President Prabowo Subianto urged Gibran to defend himself. Separately on Thursday, Indonesian police announced that they gathered enough initial evidence to pursue treason charges against four suspects accused of wiretapping Prabowo. Former police chief Listyo Sigit Prabowo (of no relation to the president) and three senior police officials were arrested last week over suspicion that they monitored phones belonging to President Prabowo, other government officials, activists, and journalists. Listyo Prabowo was a close advisor to President Prabowo. Former senior Bolivian judge arrested on suspicion of drug trafficking: On Wednesday, Bolivian authorities Aldo Quezada, the former chief justice of the Santa Cruz departmental court, on suspicion of drug trafficking. He resigned last month after the U.S. restricted his visa over alleged links to drug traffickers. The U.S. government's visa-restrictions list has also targeted officials in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru. Quezada is one of several senior Bolivian judicial officials arrested since September. Former Attorney General Roger Mariaca was arrested on September 30 on suspicion of money laundering and drug trafficking. Right-wing President Rodrigo Paz, who took office in November 2025, has sought closer ties with the U.S. Last month, Drop Site's Jose Luis Granada Ceja reported on the arrest of Mariaca and the selective use of drug-trafficking accusations to advance U.S. interests in Latin America. Read the full story. Sudanese military leader meets with heads of state from Turkey, Pakistan, and Libya at climate summit: Sudanese army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan with Turkish President Recep Erdogan, Pakistani President Shehbaz Sharif, and Libyan Prime Minister Abdulhamid Dbeibah on the sidelines of the COP31 climate summit in Turkey on Thursday. Al-Burhan's office said that the meetings focused on political and security issues in Sudan and diplomatic and economic relations among the countries. UN peacekeepers, South Sudanese authorities failed to prevent massacre in South Sudanese village, Amnesty says: The UN Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS) was about a March 2026 attack in Abiemnom, South Sudan, but did not reinforce its peacekeeping ranks until after the attack, Amnesty International said in a report on Thursday. As many as 1,500 armed men attacked the village of Abiemnom, shooting residents, burning more than 230 structures, and looting a hospital. More than 200 people died. After Amnesty released the report, a UNMISS spokesperson said that cuts to the UN peacekeeping force's budget required the force to concentrate on protecting about 2,500 people sheltering at its base. The spokesperson said that UNMISS repeatedly asked the South Sudanese army for more forces. The UN Security Council renewed the UNMISS mandate in April, but cut its troop count from 17,000 to 12,000. | | ---|---|--- Democrats Missed Hegseth Impeachment Vote While at a Fundraiser with Defense Lobbyists Palm Beach County's Israel Bonds Holdings Hit 24% of Portfolio Last Month 🛒 for your Drop News/Not Bombs Hoodie 💬 our Whatsapp Broadcast Channel for the latest reporting, podcasts, and breaking news, delivered directly ⚠️ You can go to your to unsubscribe from the Drop Site Daily newsletter--while still getting the rest of our reporting Become a Drop Site News Paid Subscriber Drop Site News is reader-supported. clean_body: We won because of you | | | | The stakes could not have been higher, Derek, and you showed up. It’s Gov. Tony Evers, and I gotta tell you, I was optimistic heading into Election Day, but I could never have expected these results. David Crowley defeated Tom Tiffany handily, even though David was outspent 2.5 to 1 by Tiffany’s billionaire backers. And to add a cherry on top, Democrats took back both houses of the State Legislature, giving us a Democratic trifecta in Madison for the first time in years! Derek, there are going to be a lot of pundits talking out of their you-know-where about how Democrats were able to pull off such an amazing victory. But they don’t know Wisconsin. So let me tell you how we won: 🔵 It took unity. That is why Democrats went on a 19-stop Unity Tour across the state – because we are all Democrats, and we are all in this to win. 🟢 It took teamwork, and lots of it. From knocking doors to making phone calls, volunteers outworked MAGA Republicans to get the job done. 🟡 And it took you, Derek. Yes, you! Every donation, big or small, was essential to electing David Crowley and Democrats up and down the ballot. This is how we won, and if Democrats continue to follow this playbook, we will keep winning in Wisconsin and across the country. Friend,

I promise I won’t take up much of your time.

My name is Shane Jenkins, and I founded Stand In The Gap Foundation. As one of the January 6 defendants, I watched what my fellow patriots endured: arrests, relentless transfers between facilities, prolonged solitary confinement, and families left to face the full weight of the government alone.

**Our nation’s justice system is being weaponized against ordinary Americans.** That’s why we exist: to stand in the gap for Americans facing judicial injustice, so no one has to fight the system by themselves.

Today, especially in the next sixty minutes, I want to reach as many people as I can with this request. I’ve set a goal to raise $20,000 before the end of the month to support our four initiatives under Operation Restore.

**If that is all you need to hear, please contribute $10 or whatever you can afford using this button:**
[Support Stand In The Gap Foundation](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckD1uxCAUhE-DO1v8eP1TUERaudu0KdEzPNsoGBC83Vw_8kq5QNqZ0eib-XqYB_jg4_4JJ-pCmynVDLyiTdFVSpUgOh_pwB2ykVwOrRCtUAYs-ReaHhqnnXUgbINajHN_m8b-NjeHBslXyzcxWhBqHGFdp2mae2X7Ca3k0Hh99QkhlBgUv43dNDmUgM7xbZ35vLKeQ8BCXcH8XIO3EAnq95aKxc6mswn6IMqVqQ8mFyaXivZZsIOILtGVuLRrQetjSwe2O2QmlwzthZ8iU8uTTmPhzOD3yNT9j4jJ4e2kSBiJqXuhrSna5R8fgq_DyHq-n-DDm4P-99xLy98AAAD__1eEfq4)
**Otherwise, let me explain why I’m asking you to give at least $10 to our four initiatives:**

[$10 because Stand for Justice](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckD1uxCAUhE-DO1v8eP1TUERaudu0KdEzPNsoGBC83Vw_8kq5QNqZ0eib-XqYB_jg4_4JJ-pCmynVDLyiTdFVSpUgOh_pwB2ykVwOrRCtUAYs-ReaHhqnnXUgbINajHN_m8b-NjeHBslXyzcxWhBqHGFdp2mae2X7Ca3k0Hh99QkhlBgUv43dNDmUgM7xbZ35vLKeQ8BCXcH8XIO3EAnq95aKxc6mswn6IMqVqQ8mFyaXivZZsIOILtGVuLRrQetjSwe2O2QmlwzthZ8iU8uTTmPhzOD3yNT9j4jJ4e2kSBiJqXuhrSna5R8fgq_DyHq-n-DDm4P-99xLy98AAAD__1eEfq4) provides legal defense, hardship relief, and record sealing for January 6 defendants and others prosecuted for who they are rather than what they did.

[$10 because Bring My Baby Home](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckD1uxCAUhE-DO1v8eP1TUERaudu0KdEzPNsoGBC83Vw_8kq5QNqZ0eib-XqYB_jg4_4JJ-pCmynVDLyiTdFVSpUgOh_pwB2ykVwOrRCtUAYs-ReaHhqnnXUgbINajHN_m8b-NjeHBslXyzcxWhBqHGFdp2mae2X7Ca3k0Hh99QkhlBgUv43dNDmUgM7xbZ35vLKeQ8BCXcH8XIO3EAnq95aKxc6mswn6IMqVqQ8mFyaXivZZsIOILtGVuLRrQetjSwe2O2QmlwzthZ8iU8uTTmPhzOD3yNT9j4jJ4e2kSBiJqXuhrSna5R8fgq_DyHq-n-DDm4P-99xLy98AAAD__1eEfq4) helps parents fight to bring home children taken by a system that never should have taken them in the first place.

[$10 because Restore Honor](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckD1uxCAUhE-DO1v8eP1TUERaudu0KdEzPNsoGBC83Vw_8kq5QNqZ0eib-XqYB_jg4_4JJ-pCmynVDLyiTdFVSpUgOh_pwB2ykVwOrRCtUAYs-ReaHhqnnXUgbINajHN_m8b-NjeHBslXyzcxWhBqHGFdp2mae2X7Ca3k0Hh99QkhlBgUv43dNDmUgM7xbZ35vLKeQ8BCXcH8XIO3EAnq95aKxc6mswn6IMqVqQ8mFyaXivZZsIOILtGVuLRrQetjSwe2O2QmlwzthZ8iU8uTTmPhzOD3yNT9j4jJ4e2kSBiJqXuhrSna5R8fgq_DyHq-n-DDm4P-99xLy98AAAD__1eEfq4) protects service members who were unjustly punished by the very system they swore to defend.

[$10 because Protect Freedom](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckD1uxCAUhE-DO1v8eP1TUERaudu0KdEzPNsoGBC83Vw_8kq5QNqZ0eib-XqYB_jg4_4JJ-pCmynVDLyiTdFVSpUgOh_pwB2ykVwOrRCtUAYs-ReaHhqnnXUgbINajHN_m8b-NjeHBslXyzcxWhBqHGFdp2mae2X7Ca3k0Hh99QkhlBgUv43dNDmUgM7xbZ35vLKeQ8BCXcH8XIO3EAnq95aKxc6mswn6IMqVqQ8mFyaXivZZsIOILtGVuLRrQetjSwe2O2QmlwzthZ8iU8uTTmPhzOD3yNT9j4jJ4e2kSBiJqXuhrSna5R8fgq_DyHq-n-DDm4P-99xLy98AAAD__1eEfq4) helps seniors and vulnerable adults stripped of their rights by the courts that were meant to protect them.

Different courtrooms, same pattern: an ordinary American up against the full weight of the state, with nobody standing beside them. Donations from people like you change that.

**When a family walks into that courtroom with someone in their corner, know it was your support today that made the difference.**

[Can I count on you to contribute $10, or whatever you can afford today, to help us stand beside more Americans facing a weaponized justice system? Click any button below to give today.](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckD1uxCAUhE-DO1v8eP1TUERaudu0KdEzPNsoGBC83Vw_8kq5QNqZ0eib-XqYB_jg4_4JJ-pCmynVDLyiTdFVSpUgOh_pwB2ykVwOrRCtUAYs-ReaHhqnnXUgbINajHN_m8b-NjeHBslXyzcxWhBqHGFdp2mae2X7Ca3k0Hh99QkhlBgUv43dNDmUgM7xbZ35vLKeQ8BCXcH8XIO3EAnq95aKxc6mswn6IMqVqQ8mFyaXivZZsIOILtGVuLRrQetjSwe2O2QmlwzthZ8iU8uTTmPhzOD3yNT9j4jJ4e2kSBiJqXuhrSna5R8fgq_DyHq-n-DDm4P-99xLy98AAAD__1eEfq4)

clean_body: I promise I won’t take up much of your time. | | | |ARCHIVE| | | Friend, I promise I won’t take up much of your time. My name is Shane Jenkins, and I founded Stand In The Gap Foundation. As one of the January 6 defendants, I watched what my fellow patriots endured: arrests, relentless transfers between facilities, prolonged solitary confinement, and families left to face the full weight of the government alone. Our nation’s justice system is being weaponized against ordinary Americans. That’s why we exist: to stand in the gap for Americans facing judicial injustice, so no one has to fight the system by themselves. Today, especially in the next sixty minutes, I want to reach as many people as I can with this request. I’ve set a goal to raise $20,000 before the end of the month to support our four initiatives under Operation Restore. If that is all you need to hear, please contribute $10 or whatever you can afford using this button: Otherwise, let me explain why I’m asking you to give at least $10 to our four initiatives: provides legal defense, hardship relief, and record sealing for January 6 defendants and others prosecuted for who they are rather than what they did. helps parents fight to bring home children taken by a system that never should have taken them in the first place. protects service members who were unjustly punished by the very system they swore to defend. helps seniors and vulnerable adults stripped of their rights by the courts that were meant to protect them. Different courtrooms, same pattern: an ordinary American up against the full weight of the state, with nobody standing beside them. Donations from people like you change that. When a family walks into that courtroom with someone in their corner, know it was your support today that made the difference. Thank you for standing in the gap, Shane Jenkins Co-founder & Initiative Coordinator Stand In The Gap Foundation P.S. If you’re still reading this email, but I haven’t convinced you to give at least $10 today, think about who the system comes for when no one is watching : Patriots prosecuted for their beliefs Parents fighting to bring their children home Veterans punished by the country they served Seniors stripped of their freedom in an afternoon The Founders built a justice system to protect citizens from government overreach. When that system is turned against the people it was meant to protect, someone has to stand in the gap. For just $10, you can be that someone. | | Has it sunk in yet, team? **The American people have delivered a thorough, historic rejection of MAGA authoritarianism and Republican extremism.** You should be proud of everything you did to help make sure more voters could make their voices heard — in the face of ruthless, racist map-rigging and voter suppression attempts. Thank you for your dedication to democracy as a member of the Fair Fight team. Alongside supporters, donors, and volunteers from across the country, you helped deliver sweeping victories up and down the ballot. These wins were years in the making. Since our founding after the 2018 elections, Fair Fight has pushed back against Jim Crow-style voter suppression, worked to elect Democracy Champions, and pursued the fundamental principle of equal access to the ballot box. It’s paid off. Activists like you shocked the political world by helping elect Mississippi’s first Democratic Senator in decades and first Black U.S. Senator since Reconstruction. You’ve also continued to prove that in Georgia, when we lock arms and fight side by side, we can win big. Keisha Lance Bottoms will be our next governor, flipping the seat from red to blue and becoming the first Black woman to run any state in the nation. Jon Ossoff will return to the U.S. Senate, where he will continue fighting for nationwide pro-democracy reforms and voting rights protections. Democrats swept statewide offices in Georgia. And Georgia Democrats flipped the State House for the first time in decades. We’ve believed this was possible for a long time. In 2011, Stacey Abrams became House minority leader as Republicans rigged the voting maps to try and lock in a supermajority. But, they never got it. Between 2014 and 2020, Democrats brought 800,000 new Georgians into the process. In 2018, they won 11 House seats, then gained more in every election since. This year, Fair Fight went all in with Georgia Takes the House, working alongside a strong coalition and the candidates, volunteers, grassroots donors, and voters who made this happen. Now Republicans won’t be able to redraw Georgia’s maps on their own, and Leader Carolyn Hugley is in line to become Georgia’s first Black woman Speaker. **Georgia doesn’t wait for the odds to change. We change them.** The results prove the power of a basic formula: investing in long-term organizing to expand the electorate and protect the freedom to vote. There was a time when you’d get laughed out of the room if you said Georgia would be a battleground state. (Ask me how I know.) Now it’s undeniable. **And now we can continue to apply that same formula across the South** — pressing our advantage in states that are suddenly swinging blue in the heart of the Old Confederacy, despite all the Neo-Confederate attempts to suppress Black and brown voters and cement white, one-party rule. Look at Mississippi. Look at Texas. Look at South Carolina. Look at Louisiana, Alabama, Tennessee, and Florida, where Democrats came within just a few points of victory. **The numbers are there. The commitment is there — from tireless organizers who continue to build on the legacy of generations of freedom fighters. Together, we’ll keep fighting to make sure no one counts out the South.** Now let’s march forward. Thank you, Lauren Groh-Wargo

clean_body: You should be proud of everything you did to make sure more voters could make their voices heard. | | | Has it sunk in yet, team? The American people have delivered a thorough, historic rejection of MAGA authoritarianism and Republican extremism. You should be proud of everything you did to help make sure more voters could make their voices heard — in the face of ruthless, racist map-rigging and voter suppression attempts. Thank you for your dedication to democracy as a member of the Fair Fight team. Alongside supporters, donors, and volunteers from across the country, you helped deliver sweeping victories up and down the ballot. These wins were years in the making. Since our founding after the 2018 elections, Fair Fight has pushed back against Jim Crow-style voter suppression, worked to elect Democracy Champions, and pursued the fundamental principle of equal access to the ballot box. It’s paid off. Activists like you shocked the political world by helping elect Mississippi’s first Democratic Senator in decades and first Black U.S. Senator since Reconstruction. You’ve also continued to prove that in Georgia, when we lock arms and fight side by side, we can win big. Keisha Lance Bottoms will be our next governor, flipping the seat from red to blue and becoming the first Black woman to run any state in the nation. Jon Ossoff will return to the U.S. Senate, where he will continue fighting for nationwide pro-democracy reforms and voting rights protections. Democrats swept statewide offices in Georgia. And Georgia Democrats flipped the State House for the first time in decades. We’ve believed this was possible for a long time. In 2011, Stacey Abrams became House minority leader as Republicans rigged the voting maps to try and lock in a supermajority. But, they never got it. Between 2014 and 2020, Democrats brought 800,000 new Georgians into the process. In 2018, they won 11 House seats, then gained more in every election since. This year, Fair Fight went all in with Georgia Takes the House, working alongside a strong coalition and the candidates, volunteers, grassroots donors, and voters who made this happen. Now Republicans won’t be able to redraw Georgia’s maps on their own, and Leader Carolyn Hugley is in line to become Georgia’s first Black woman Speaker. Georgia doesn’t wait for the odds to change. We change them. The results prove the power of a basic formula: investing in long-term organizing to expand the electorate and protect the freedom to vote. There was a time when you’d get laughed out of the room if you said Georgia would be a battleground state. (Ask me how I know.) Now it’s undeniable. And now we can continue to apply that same formula across the South — pressing our advantage in states that are suddenly swinging blue in the heart of the Old Confederacy, despite all the Neo-Confederate attempts to suppress Black and brown voters and cement white, one-party rule. Look at Mississippi. Look at Texas. Look at South Carolina. Look at Louisiana, Alabama, Tennessee, and Florida, where Democrats came within just a few points of victory. The numbers are there. The commitment is there — from tireless organizers who continue to build on the legacy of generations of freedom fighters. Together, we’ll keep fighting to make sure no one counts out the South. Now let’s march forward. Thank you, Lauren Groh-Wargo CEO, Fair Fight | | = = | 1270 Caroline Street | Suite D120-430 | Atlanta, GA 30307 ©2026 Fair Fight - All rights reserved. ## **New Leaders, Same Blind Spot: Why Republicans Haven 't Heart the Voters**
This week on Capitol Hill, House and Senate Republicans held their leadership elections to chart the path forward for the next Congress.
In the Senate, Republicans opted for complete continuity, reelecting their entire slate from last cycle - with Sen. John Thune remaining at the helm as he transitions into the role of Minority Leader. Over in the House, lawmakers shook things up by electing Ohio Rep. Jim Jordan over current Majority Leader Steve Scalise in a 106-73 secret ballot.

Thune reelected as Senate GOP leader after brutal midterm losses
| |
| 9:01 PM * Nov 10, 2026 * 10.3K Views143 Replies * 20 Reposts * 54 Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/cd9eb68a-1b5e-4492-b3af-ba4235504377?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Both leaders immediately laid out how they plan to operate in the minority and go on offense against the incoming Democratic majorities. Fighting back against Democratic overreach and oversight battles is necessary - especially when the pressure mounts.
**But there is a massive piece missing from the equation: a real vision for the future.**
Voters sent an unmistakable message at the ballot box last week. They told us that daily life has become too expensive - from housing and energy bills to groceries and healthcare. Yet, when you ask people in Washington what Republicans are focused on right now, the answer you keep hearing is "permitting reform."

subject: After the election: What now for Forward?

body:
Join our National Volunteer Call next Tues for updates on how election night went.

| | [ ](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=JgyyvCfQwldlSeD7KJl_Ih7269o_4hwqOhPs1_PHvgI&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=forward_friends_nov_26&n=1)
---
| Hello Forward Friends- I don't know about you, but to me election night is very special, it reminds me of New Year's. On both nights you stay up late excitedly, and the morning brings new beginnings. This year America made history electing minority women. Unfortunately, though the pendulum of power just swung to the other side, with no change to the systems that got us here in the first place. Thus, our work continues! We had **38** Forward endorsed candidates win, with 3 of those being Independents elected to their state legislatures. Our federal level candidates pulled historic vote totals. If you like to hear more about our wins and what we accomplished this cycle, join our _National Volunteer Call_ this **Tues Nov 17th at 7:30pm ET** for an election recap. | [](https://home.forwardparty.com/national_volunteer_call_20261013_20261110?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=forward_friends_nov_26&n=2 "RSVP FOR THE CALL") [RSVP FOR THE CALL](https://home.forwardparty.com/national_volunteer_call_20261013_20261110?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=forward_friends_nov_26&n=2)
---
**_Text Banking Stats_**
Thanks to about 50 amazing volunteers, we were able to send out over **360,000** texts in support of **26** candidates. That's 100,000 more texts than we sent out in 2024! Special appreciation to our top 5 texters, **Wylene Small** with 82,126, **Ashley Rivera** with 75,860, **Jeanne Sole** with 60,744, **Kris Sun** with 41,325, and **Julie Brustman** with 35,763 texts sent. You guys are amazing! ** __**
**_Volunteer Spotlight_**
We had so many people who stepped up this election season. One story in particular was really moving. Our volunteer of the month, **Juli Servatius** **from MN** , was a total rockstar, and traveled to knock on doors with us in both South Carolina and South Dakota! While in SC she met **Kayla Sullivan** , our other volunteer of the month, who was a campaign manager for some local races there. Juli introduced Kayla to a Forward candidate needing help in MN, and Kayla jumped right in. It's so inspiring to see our supporters connecting across states to make a difference! Thank you, Juli and Kayla, for your dedication to this movement.
**Tues Nov 17th @ 7:30 pm ET** \- [National Volunteer Call](https://home.forwardparty.com/national_volunteer_call_20261013_20261110?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=forward_friends_nov_26&n=3)
* Election recap edition! Join us for an overview of the party and how to use our website for volunteer resources. In this edition we will also talk about how our candidates did this election.

**Wed Dec 2nd @ 6:30pm ET** \- [Welcome Team Training](https://home.forwardparty.com/welcome_team_intro_call_20261012_20261202?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=forward_friends_nov_26&n=4)
* Learn how to call other Forward supporters in your state and welcome them to the party! Script and template provided.

**Wed Dec 9nd @ 6:30pm ET** \- [Run for Office Webinar](https://home.forwardparty.com/run_for_office_dec_26?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=forward_friends_nov_26&n=5)
* Are you ready to get in on the action? Learn how to get started and apply for the Forward endorsement at our webinar!

I had amazing time this election season. It was incredible to meet so many of you in person. The election may be over, but the party building never stops. Thank you so much to those of you who got involved this year- and if this wasn't your year to play a part, I look forward to plugging you in next year.
With gratitude,
Carrie Anne
